articles.title: Santamaría, un 'espía' en la URSS
articles.standfirst: La leyenda del Madrid se estrenó como entrenador del Espanyol en la primera gira de un club de nuestro país en la Unión Soviética para vigilar lo que le esperaba
articles.summary: La leyenda del Madrid se estrenó como entrenador del Espanyol en la primera gira de un club de nuestro país en la Unión Soviética para vigilar lo que le esperaba
articles.body: El calendario, y el Mundial, han querido que el inicio de la temporada 2026-27 cruce a Espanyol y Real Madrid. Son los dos clubes que une en España la vida de José Emilio Santamaría. Fallecido el pasado 15 de abril a los 96 años, fue leyenda madridista en el Madrid apoteósico de Di Stéfano y luego dejó su huella en el banquillo catalán al llevarlo en 1973 a ser tercero de la Liga. Ese es el tope perico, alcanzado tres veces más: 1933, 1967 y 1987. El caminar de Santamaría como entrenador solo conoce tres etapas. La primera fue muy breve, en las categorías inferiores del Real Madrid después de despedirse del fútbol en 1966. No jugó la final de la Sexta, la del Madrid ye-yé, pero sí estuvo en el camino que llevó a los blancos a la final de Bruselas: ante Kilmarnock y Feyenoord. De la Ciudad Deportiva pasó a la selección, donde dirigió al equipo olímpico en México 1970. Como lo haría en los de 1980, los de Moscú, antes de ponerse al mando de la absoluta en una etapa que supuso una de las grandes frustraciones de nuestro fútbol y de su vida: el Mundial de España de 1982. En medio de esas dos etapas como entrenador de la selección española, Santamaría experimentó lo que es entrenar día a día en la élite, en el Espanyol. La llegada de Santamaría al equipo entonces de Sarriá fue en junio de 1971. El mes anterior había estado al mando del equipo español que peleaba por estar en los Juegos de Múnich. Eliminada Turquía (3-0 y 0-0) con Santamaría al frente, el sueño se acabó en la segunda fase ante Polonia y Bulgaria, donde España solo sumó un punto. Por el camino, la selección cambió de timonel: se fue Santamaría y llegó Rial. El relevo se produjo después de que las relaciones de la directiva del Espanyol con su entrenador saltaran por los aires. A sus 60 años, Fernando Daucik era una institución en España. Nacido en la Eslovaquia de hoy (Šahy), había hecho campeón al Barcelona y al Athletic, y entrenado en el Metropolitano, en el Sevilla, en el Zaragoza... Una institución. Fue la apuesta perica para la temporada del regreso a Primera después de un fugaz paso de una temporada en Segunda. La campaña fue discreta y las tensiones entre directivos y entrenador se sucedieron. El desenlace de esa Liga fue tremendo. El Valencia, líder con 43 puntos, visitaba al Espanyol. Sus perseguidores, Atlético de Madrid (41) y Barcelona (42), chocaban en Madrid. En su partido mil en Primera y con récord de recaudación (cinco millones de pesetas), el Espanyol ganó 1-0 al Valencia. Pero la Liga se fue a Mestalla, porque en Madrid empataron a uno. Esas tablas hicieron que Daucik llamara ingenuos a rojiblancos y culés, lo que no sentó nada bien en la directiva del Espanyol después de una semana rodeada de rumores de primas. Para disparar más la tensión, desde la directiva del Espanyol se contó que el entrenador había recibido la orden tajante de no alinear ante el Valencia a su hijo, Yanko. El entrenador concentró al delantero en Sant Andreu de Llavaneres, a lo que también se oponía el club. Yanko no jugó, pero la ruptura era un hecho. Daucik dejaba al Espanyol en Primera. Sobraban las presentaciones para Santamaría e Iriondo. Después de alguna duda de fondo salarial, el 12 de mayo se cerró el compromiso de Santamaría con el Espanyol. Y con carácter inmediato, porque se decidió que el nuevo entrenador viajara con el equipo a la Unión Soviética. Nunca antes un equipo español se había adentrado en el país de los soviets, en el corazón de las naciones comunistas. Al igual que sucedió con Sudamérica, el Espanyol era pionero. Kiev (Dinamo), Leningrado (Zenit) y Moscú (Torpedo) eran las paradas. Santamaría, que fue presentado al equipo en la capital de Ucrania el lunes 1 de junio, se sumó para analizar de cerca lo que tenía: un espía reconocido. Durante la gira soviética, el Espanyol tuvo como entrenador a Pepe Mauri, leyenda de la casa perica. Santamaría tomaba nota de cara a una etapa que iba a durar hasta diciembre de 1977 y de la que aún hoy se habla con mucho cariño en la casa perica.

articles.title: Arteta no renuncia al sueño de tener a Julián Alvarez en el Arsenal
articles.standfirst: El técnico está contento con la plantilla que tiene, pero es consciente de que la llegada del argentina la mejoraría aún más
articles.summary: El técnico está contento con la plantilla que tiene, pero es consciente de que la llegada del argentina la mejoraría aún más
articles.body: El Arsenal es el rival a batir en Inglaterra. Los 'gunners' son los vigentes campeones con una plantilla muy completa, pero su entrenador, Mikel Arteta, no renuncia a mejorarla un poco más. Y ahí es cuando entra el nombre de Julián Alvarez. El delantero argentino parece destinado a continuar en el Atlético de Madrid a tenor de las últimas palabras de Gil Marín, pero la respuesta del agente del jugador podría cambiar las cosas. La tensión se respira en el ambiente colchonero y esa es la esperanza que tiene Arteta para que haya un bombazo en el final de mercado. Tras ganar en su estreno liguero ante el Coventry (3-0), el técnico español fue preguntado por la posibilidad de fichar al argentino. Sin entrar en nombres, Arteta aseguró estar feliz con los jugadores que tiene: "Estoy realmente contento con el equipo que tenemos". Sin embargo, el entrenador es consciente de que siempre se puede mejorar. "El enfoque principal es mejorar a los jugadores que ya tenemos porque ya tenemos muchas cosas buenas", dijo al término del partido, dejando abierta la puerta al ariete del Atlético, cuyo nombre seguirá sonando hasta el último día de mercado, el 1 de septiembre.

articles.title: Flick: "¿Balde? Es importante saber si un jugador está convencido para poder competir en su demarcación"
articles.standfirst: El técnico no cierra la puerta de salida
articles.summary: El técnico no cierra la puerta de salida
articles.body: HHansi Flick no cerró la puerta a posibles salidas del Barcelona. Además de los casos ya conocidos de Héctor Fort y Marc Casadó, que continúan buscando destino en esta recta final del mercado de fichajes, el técnico alemán dejó un mensaje claro al ser preguntado directamente por el futuro de Alejandro Balde. "Es una cuestión difícil porque tiene una enorme calidad y es importante saber si un jugador está convencido para poder competir en su demarcación. Eso es lo que quiero ver de todos mis jugadores", dijo el preparador. Incluso, Flick insistió en su respuesta. "Cada día veo lo que hacen los jugadores, el nivel, si me demuestran que tienen en el nivel para jugar. Al final, hay que jugar como equipo, solo entonces tendremos éxitos. Necesito que todos estén cien por cien", aseveró. Solo restan 11 días para el cierre de mercado y, por lo tanto, Balde y el Barcelona deberán tomar una decisión de forma inminente. Además, no hay que olvidar que Cancelo, que firmó el jueves, le quitó la titularidad cuando llegó en el mercado de invierno de la temporada pasada.  "Puede haber cambios y habrá que esperar hasta el final de la ventana de fichajes", afirmó Hansi Flick. Por lo tanto, aún restan días muy intensos de mercado para el Barcelona.

articles.title: Laporta retoma su agenda y estará en Elche
articles.standfirst: El presidente sufrió una arritmia a finales de julio y no pudo viajar durante la pretemporada
articles.summary: El presidente sufrió una arritmia a finales de julio y no pudo viajar durante la pretemporada
articles.body: Joan Laporta ya puede retomar con normalidad su agenda institucional después de superar la arritmia que sufrió a finales de julio. El presidente del Barcelona tiene previsto viajar este domingo a Elche para acompañar al equipo en su estreno en LaLiga y volver a ejercer plenamente sus funciones al frente de la entidad. Laporta recibió el alta médica el pasado 31 de julio tras unos días hospitalizados y, desde entonces, ha ido recuperando progresivamente su actividad habitual. Sin embargo, no había podido acompañar al conjunto azulgrana durante la pretemporada, en la que el Barça jugó en Inglaterra, Italia y Suiza. Laporta, no obstante, ya recupera la normalidad. El abogado tiene previsto participar en la tradicional comida de directivas previa al encuentro y, posteriormente, presenciará el debut liguero del Barcelona desde el palco del estadio ilicitano. Será, por tanto, su primera presencia junto al equipo fuera de la Ciudad Condal desde que sufrió el episodio cardíaco.

articles.title: Infantino Defies FIFA Vice President by Going to Youth Event in Caribbean amid Global Soccer Rift
articles.summary: GENEVA (AP) — Gianni Infantino defied a request by one of his FIFA vice presidents to stay away from an Under-14 soccer event in the Caribbean and instead made a rare public appearance during the global furor over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.
articles.body:
GENEVA (AP) — Gianni Infantino defied a request by one of his FIFA vice presidents to stay away from an Under-14 soccer event in the Caribbean and instead made a rare public appearance during the global furor over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.

On Saturday, Infantino posted photos on his Instagram account showing the FIFA president meeting political and soccer officials from the Dominican Republic on the sidelines of a Caribbean Football Union (CFU) youth tournament in the Punta Cana resort.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

On Friday, Infantino had been asked not to go by Victor Montagliani, the Canadian president of Miami-based continental soccer body CONCACAF, to avoid being a distraction from the soccer games.

"I believe that considering the governance crisis surrounding FIFA as a result of your controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, the media will focus on this situation," Montagliani wrote in an emailed letter seen by The Associated Press, "which will unfortunately significantly take away from the technical nature of the CFU youth competition."

"As such, I respectfully ask you in the name of football to reconsider your attendance as it will unfortunately undermine the technical nature of this important youth development activity," Montagliani wrote.

FIFA declined to comment on the Montagliani request, though noted it directly funds regional bodies like the CFU with up to $5 million from each four-year World Cup cycle.

Montagliani has aligned with fellow FIFA vice presidents Aleksander Ceferin from European body UEFA and Asian Football Confederation president Sheik Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa in seeking to end Infantino's increasingly executive presidency now in its 11th year.

They accused Infantino two weeks ago of "deception" in secretly planning over the past year to spin off FIFA's multi-billion dollar commercial activities to a subsidiary 20% owned by investors led by Joshua Kushner.

Infantino withdrew the project on Aug. 1 amid a global backlash by soccer leaders and fans, and hours after his own chief operating officer published stinging criticism of the proposal and his leadership style in a statement to the AP. The Zurich-based COO, Kevin Lamour, was fired this week .

Caribbean member federations are seen as potential supporters for Infantino to peel away from their CONCACAF leadership. South American body CONMEBOL has backed Infantino as its best path to hosting more games at the 2030 World Cup it wants expanded from 48 teams to 64.

The FIFA leader has not taken questions publicly since the $20 billion FFE project was revealed July 28 by British daily The Times, and on Friday in Punta Cana he evaded a reporter from British broadcaster Sky News.

Asked by Sky reporter James Matthews if he had betrayed the sport and should resign, Infantino said "Thank you so much" and made quips about both men being bald.

Infantino is aiming to be re-elected for a fourth and final term in office through 2031 at the FIFA election congress next March in Rabat, Morocco. FIFA has set Nov. 18 as a deadline for would-be candidates to enter the race.

articles.title: Marotta cierra la puerta a la salida de Lautaro: "No hay condiciones para que abandone el Inter"
articles.standfirst: El presidente 'nerazzurro' se muestra tajante sobre el futuro del argentino y asegura que el club no contempla su salida rumbo al Barça
articles.summary: El presidente 'nerazzurro' se muestra tajante sobre el futuro del argentino y asegura que el club no contempla su salida rumbo al Barça
articles.body: El presidente del Inter, Giuseppe Marotta, ha cerrado la puerta a una posible salida de Lautaro Martínez rumbo al Barcelona. El dirigente nerazzurro se mostró tajante al ser preguntado por los rumores que vinculan al delantero argentino con el conjunto azulgrana y aseguró que el club no contempla su marcha. "Lautaro es nuestro capitán y representa la historia actual del Inter. Puedo decir que no hay condiciones para que abandone el Inter. No queremos renunciar a él por ningún motivo, no tiene sentido ni siquiera hablar de ello", afirmó Marotta, dejando claro que el argentino continúa siendo una pieza fundamental en el proyecto 'nerazzurro'. El Inter abrirá la temporada 2026-27 en el Giuseppe Meazza ante el Monza, con Lautaro partiendo como titular junto a Pio Esposito en la doble punta. Un once en el que, de momento, fichajes como John Stones y Aleksandar Stankovic esperarán su oportunidad en el banquillo. Djed Spence y la reciente incorporación Curtis Jones, por su parte, no han entrado en esta primera convocatoria. Sobre la planificación de la plantilla, el presidente del Inter destacó el trabajo realizado por la dirección deportiva y aseguró que el equipo ya cuenta con suficiente potencial. "Con Ausilio y Baccin, estamos atentos a aprovechar cualquier oportunidad, consultando también con el entrenador. Junto con la actual directiva, hemos realizado nuevas inversiones: puedo decir que esta plantilla es competitiva tal como está", señaló.

Djed Spence y la reciente incorporación Curtis Jones, por su parte, no han entrado en esta primera convocatoria. Sobre la planificación de la plantilla, el presidente del Inter destacó el trabajo realizado por la dirección deportiva y aseguró que el equipo ya cuenta con suficiente potencial. "Con Ausilio y Baccin, estamos atentos a aprovechar cualquier oportunidad, consultando también con el entrenador. Junto con la actual directiva, hemos realizado nuevas inversiones: puedo decir que esta plantilla es competitiva tal como está", señaló.

articles.title: Spurs coach De Zerbi must find a way to cure losing mentality
articles.summary: Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi discovers cash is no cure for a losing mentality as they crash to a heavy defeat at Brentford, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi may have spent close to Â£400m by the time his Tottenham Hotspur rebuild is complete â but it took just his side's first Premier League game of the season to prove all the money in the world is no guaranteed cure for a losing mentality.

De Zerbi, by his own admission, confirmed his role was more psychologist than coach when he was given seven games to keep Spurs in the top-flight following his appointment in March.

He achieved that feat, but only just as Spurs survived with victory against Everton on the final day.

The Italian has been handed vast funds for a host of new players to ensure Spurs do not suffer a repeat of the nightmare campaign.

This dreadful defeat was not the start he or the Spurs power brokers envisaged.

For all the change in transfer strategy and personnel, the manner in which Spurs capitulated at the first sign of pressure as they were run ragged by Brentford provided gruesome evidence that you need more than a huge transfer fund to give a team mental strength.

De Zerbi may feel he has addressed some of the ills in a squad that has finished 17th in the Premier League two seasons in succession. However, he will have to turn psychologist once more as the new Spurs looked like the old Spurs as they were dismantled in the west London sunshine.

He pointed to a lack of physical conditioning of players who had been at the World Cup or were newcomers, but this did not excuse the lack of basics, shortage of resilience and the fact Brentford were so superior in every area.

De Zerbi told BBC Sport's Match of the Day: "Bad game. We lost and suffered the difference in the duels. It was the key of this game. We didn't fight in the right way. Maybe credit to them because it's the best quality Brentford have.

"Our physical condition was not in the right level for all players because many came later after the World Cup and there were many new players in the squad and first XI. But we have to analyse this game better because we can't play this way in this type of game."

The day started with Spurs fans bursting with optimism in one corner of The Gtech Community Stadium, welcoming their new recruits raucously. It ended with those same players applauding a large swathe of empty seats, some vacating as early as the 49th minute when Michael Kayode put The Bees 3-0 up.

It could have been even worse had the normally reliable Igor Thiago not struck the post with a penalty, but that was no consolation for Spurs or De Zerbi on what was a chastening day.

Rock superstar Jon Bon Jovi was an interested spectator at The Gtech Stadium - and Spurs gave him enough material for several albums worth of sad power ballads as they started badly and went into rapid decline.

De Zerbi gave debuts to four of his new acquisitions in Andrew Robertson, Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali. They will feel the only way is up because they were at rock bottom here. None of them distinguished themselves, although neither did any others.

Italian midfielder Tonali cost Â£100m from Newcastle United , but was utterly outshone and overpowered by Brentford 's record buy Mamadou Sangare, who was the game's outstanding performer.

Tonali's only memorable contribution was a first-half attempt on goal that flew horribly skywards, prompting the inevitable suggestion from Brentford supporters that Spurs had wasted their money.

Matheus Fernades, at Â£85m from West Ham United, came on as a substitute, while Savinho and possibly Omar Marmoush will add strength, but it was the lack of heart and fight that will be De Zerbi's biggest concern.

From the first minute, Spurs' brave new world hauntingly resembled the old one as they cracked under the first sign of pressure, Brentford sensing their weakness as they hunted down a side they clearly felt could be exposed.

Brentford should have been ahead before Keane Lewis-Potter broke the deadlock after 12 minutes, the contest effectively over when Vitaly Janelt doubled their lead before half-time.

De Zerbi cut a frustrated, animated figure as he tried to enliven Spurs, but heads were down, physical challenges lost, desperation their trademark, with not the slightest indication of any self-belief that they might recover the situation.

Conor Gallagher and Lucas Bergvall did not return after the half-time interval, although they might justifiably point out others could have accompanied them.

De Zerbi somehow needs to get into the heads of these Spurs players to give them strength and steel. That is not something that can be achieved with a wave of the chequebook.

For context, this is Spurs' first game of the Premier League season and many teams with aspiration and ambition have had nightmare starts.

This, however, looked like the worrying continuation of a pattern of defeat and despair.

That pattern has cast a cloud over Spurs' recent seasons, along with De Zerbi's predecessors Ange Postecoglou, who at least won the Europa League, then Thomas Frank and â in his "blink and you'll miss it" reign â Igor Tudor.

De Zerbi added: "I am surprised for the result and performance. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can't find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance. We are starting a new project and we couldn't find the principle.

"Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things like organisation and pressing."

More signings may be on the way, but De Zerbi said: "I don't want the excuse that the first XI was not enough to compete and get a result. Brentford 's spirit on the pitch was great, it has to be the right example for us."

New faces are all very well, but this loss showed Spurs problems run deeper than fresh personnel. De Zerbi must banish the ghosts of two seasons littered with losses. And quickly.

He must not change his squad. He must change a culture in which defeats like this have become commonplace.

articles.title: "El balón de playa" a Vinicius lanza al Espanyol al empate
articles.standfirst: El brasileño se enfrentó con la grada y elevó el clima momentos antes del empate
articles.summary: El brasileño se enfrentó con la grada y elevó el clima momentos antes del empate
articles.body: "Balón de playa, Vinicius balón de playa". El cántico atronó en el estadio del Espanyol cuando, poco antes de la media hora, el brasileño se encaró en una jugada con Riedel. De ese choque con el central alemán nació un gesto de Vinicius hacia la afición del Espanyol. La respuesta fue el famoso cántico surgido a raíz del caso del Balón de Oro que acabó en manos de Rodri. De ese incendio en la grada nació una fase del partido que pocos minutos después acabó con el gol de Álex Calatrava y la explosión de la grada espanyolista. Un par de acciones en las que Vinicius anduvo más pendiente de esa guerra que de leer el ataque del Espanyol generaron ventajas para los de Manolo González La tensión con el brasileño se vivió casi desde el inicio. A los tres minutos llegó el primer roce, con Calatrava. El 7 del Madrid se quejó de una patada a destiempo del jugador del Espanyol. A ese primer revuelo quiso poner orden Sánchez Martínez, llamando al orden a los dos capitanes. Pero la mecha ya estaba prendida.. Después del gol, a los 32 minutos, el árbitro marcó el límite. Otro roce con Calatrava derivó en un amago de tangana. Y Sánchez Martínez amonestó a los dos jugadores. Ambos se quejaron de la tarjeta. Como lo hacía Mourinho, al entender que cada vez que Vinicius recibía la pelota era objeto de falta. La temporada 2026-27 nace con la misma dinámica de las anteriores. La relación de Vincius con la gradas rivales no parece un asunto que se enfríe. Más bien todo lo contrario.

articles.title: Espí esconde que a Güler no se le puede cambiar
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Espanyol- Real Madrid
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Espanyol- Real Madrid
articles.body: El episodio IV del Madrid de Mourinho ya está en marcha. El RCDE Stadium fue el escenario en el que se levantó el telón de la segunda aventura del técnico portugués en la Casa Blanca. El despegue de un proyecto que arranca con la incógnita de si logrará alcanzar el éxito, como ocurrió con el regreso de Carlo Ancelotti en 2021, o si acabará dando la razón al viejo dicho español de que las segundas partes nunca fueron buenas. Ante un Espanyol que repetía en casa después de arrancar LaLiga de manera contundente (3-0 al Levante), el Madrid se encontró con dos partidos. Uno hasta la media hora, en el que fue mucho mejor; otro a partir del momento en el que Vinicius se enfrentó a la grada y encendió una chispa que prendió al equipo de Manolo González para sentirse capaz de todo a base de corazón. Pero no solo se puede mirar a Vinicius. Porque Mbappé tuvo uno de esos partidos en los que parece que la portería es de hockey sobre patines. El francés, Bota de Oro del Mundial, las tuvo de todos los colores. Pero no fue capaz de marcar. El campo del Espanyol sigue en su lista de campos en los que no ha marcado. Y no fue porque su equipo no le encontrara. Todo lo contrario que Carlos Espí. El fichaje de menor rango del Madrid fue el que resolvió el partido. Tres puntos de oro con la firma de un chaval que apunta a dar muchas cosas al Madrid... y a la selección.  Lanzó el portugués un aviso a navegantes en la previa del partido. Una especie de provocación simpática a los periodistas y un avios a quienes viven dentro de la caseta blanca: "El once ya se lo dicho a los jugadores. A ver quién de vosotros tiene mejores contactos". Truco de entrenador curtido, de saber manejar tiempos y espacios. A las 20.11 horas saltó el equipo: Courtois; Dumfries, Konaté, Huijsen, Carreras; Valverde, Bernardo Silva; Güler, Bellingham, Vinicius y Mbappé. Ese quedaba como el primer equipo de Mourinho en LaLiga, con tres de los fichajes y la BMV.  Tardó menos de 10 minutos el Madrid de Mourinho en tomar el mando del partido. De una falta lateral sacada por Vinicius, derribado hasta tres veces en los albores del partido, nació un centro de Güler al corazón del área del Espanyol. Allí apareció Bellingham para aprovechar la pasividad y colapso de la defensa del Espanyol para cabecear a la red. Su nombre aparece en la tabla de los primeros goleadores del Madrid en la Liga. Y, de paso, prolongar el excelente nivel que mostró en el Mundial. Si el 5 anda fuerte y la mezcla con Güler funciona como parece... Tenía el Madrid el partido donde quería. Bellingham campaba a sus anchas. Güler mandaba y mostraba galones de jugador dominante. Entonces no se le ocurrió otra cosa que encararse cerca de su área con un central rival, Riedel. Y después, con la grada. El cloroformo en el que tenía el Madrid al equipo de Manolo González se convirtió en adrenalina perica. Nunca se podrá demostrar si fue una situación de causa-efecto, pero el caso es que el gol del Espanyo llegó de inmediato. Y lo que era un partido en un solo sentido comenzó a vivirse en las dos áeas. No puede haber debate. Haga lo que haga Mourinho a la hora de encajar a sus piezas, el turco debe estar en el terreno de juego. Ya no es el jugador de destellos, de lagunas, de momentos superlativos y vacíos demasiado largos. No. Ahora Arda es un futbolista para entregarle los mandos del Madrid, para desbordar confianza en lo que tiene y hace. Construir alrededor de su talento será una buena apuesta. Todo lo que no sea eso apunta al error. Fue el primer cambio. Hay cosas que parecen no cambiar. El Madrid ganó, pero sin el turco tuvo mucho menos brillo. En una noche de broncas al Madrid hubo una excepción: Marc Cucurella. El campeón del mundo fue recibido con aplausos desde que se anunció su nombre entre los suplentes blancos. Saltó al campo pasada la hora de partido y se llevó una gran ovación. A un campeón del mundo, a un chico que pasó por la cantera del Espanyol, aunque luego cambiara de acera en Barcelona. Cada disputa entre ellos fue un noble cuerpo a cuerpo para registrar entre las cosas que debe hacer un delantero jugando de espaldas a la meta rival y las que debe ofrecer un central para proteger a su equipo y no verse en desventaja. El ariete del Espanyol, que venía de marcar dos goles en el estreno de Liga, se dio una paliza monumental en un partido poco agradable para un delantero. El central francés mostró argumentos para defender su fichaje y su titularidad. Para el capitán del Madrid fue un partido de brega, de mucho desgaste, de ida y vuelta. Demostró estar en el nivel de ese jugador incansable capaz de cubrir huecos allá donde sus compañeros no llegan. Las opciones para aparecer en ataque no le sobraron. Pero fue un disparo suyo, con el reloj cerca del minuto 80, el que estuvo a punto de tumbar el 1-1. Pero la madera fue su destino final.

articles.title: El Real Madrid necesitaba a Carlos Espí
articles.standfirst: Una opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.summary: Una opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.body: Pues claro que sí. El Madrid necesitaba un jugador como Carlos Espí. Tenía a Gonzalo, pero le dieron poca bola. Y desde Joselu no tenía un delantero de esas características. Y cuando lo tenía no lo ponía. Y sin delantero centro es harto complicado ganar partidos. Mbappé no lo es exactamente. Mbappé es un goleador nato. Ante el Espanyol no mojó, pero pudo hacerlo. De hecho tuvo en sus botas el 1-2. Lo evitó Dmitrovic. Pero eso fue en la primera parte. Luego, en la segunda, el Madrid tuvo más tiempo el balón que el Espanyol, pero no supo qué hacer con él. Se cansó Mourinho de lo que estaba viendo y dio entrada a Diomande, Camavinga, Trent y Carlos Espí. Dejó en el campo a Vinícius, que lo intentó mucho y desbordó poco. ¿Por qué no lo cambió Mourinho? Parece como si quisiera recuperarlo para la causa, pero de momento eso va para largo. Tampoco se entiende mucho que Arda Güler se fuese al banquillo cuando el Madrid no está sobrado de talento en el centro del campo. Bernardo Silva no estuvo mal, pero tampoco jugó como para hacerle la ola. Y Diomande dio la impresión de estar muy verde. Intentó alguna que otra cosa, pero de momento no parece haberse ganado el puesto en la banda derecha. Y, en fin, al final apareció Carlos Espí. Estaba claro que no iba a ser titular en este Madrid cargado de estrellas, pero también estaba claro que iba a jugar muchos partidos en cuanto las cosas se pusieran feas. Y al Madrid estuvo a punto de ponérsele muy feo el partido, porque empezar la Liga dejándose dos puntos en el campo del Espanyol habría sido un pinchazo muy pero que muy serio. Espí está para eso, para cazar goles. Y de entrada ya ha amortizado su fichaje.

articles.title: Nordic Soccer Associations Have 'Lost Confidence' in FIFA Boss Infantino
articles.summary: STOCKHOLM (AP) — Six Nordic national soccer associations piled more pressure on embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino on Sunday by saying they had "lost confidence" in his leadership.
articles.body:
STOCKHOLM (AP) — Six Nordic national soccer associations piled more pressure on embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino on Sunday by saying they had "lost confidence" in his leadership.

The associations from Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark, Iceland and the Faeroe Islands issued a joint statement to say they "view the organization's governance and decision-making at the highest level with great concern."

The associations said they stand united with European soccer governing body UEFA and support the measures it has already proposed.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

"We expect FIFA to provide binding guarantees that the organization's governance or competitions will never again be opened up to private ownership," the associations said.

Infantino faces pressure to resign after his plans to sell future World Cup profits to private investors triggered a backlash and criticism from UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF, the governing body for North and Central American and Caribbean soccer.

"We also support the call by AFC, CONCACAF and UEFA for a fully independent external investigation into the events surrounding the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal," the Nordic associations said.

The statement called for FIFA to "initiate a comprehensive and independent review of its governance framework" to see whether it is adhering to the "independence, checks and balances, transparency and accountability that were intended when FIFA adopted its reform program in 2016."

articles.title: Women's Super League: Australians are seen widely in WSL but why not Premier League?
articles.summary: The Premier League used to feature a host of top Australians. Now there is just one player from the country in the competition, but it's a very different story in the WSL.
articles.body:
The Premier League used to feature plenty of Australian talent.

Mark Schwarzer played 514 Premier League games â more than any of his compatriots â while Lucas Neill, Harry Kewell, Brett Emerton, Tim Cahill, Mark Viduka, Mark Bosnich, Mat Ryan, Aaron Mooy and Mile Jedinak all established themselves in England's top flight.

But while there are a number of Australians in the men's Championship, the Premier League has just one representative.

Lucas Herrington, 18, recently joined promoted Hull City from Colorado Rapids in a deal believed to be worth about Â£17m including add-ons. , external

The picture is very different in the Women's Super League.

There are 13 Australians across eight clubs, including three at Arsenal and three at promoted Charlton Athletic.

So why has England's top women's division become a magnet for Australian players, while the path to the Premier League has become less well-trodden?

Matildas head coach Joe Montemurro suggests one factor is that more men's players are staying in Australia.

So while there are still Australians coming to England to play - such as Portsmouth's Hayden Matthews and Thomas Waddingham, Norwich's Mohamed Toure, Middlesbrough's Riley McGree and Blackburn's Lewis Miller, Montemurro suggests that many more who might have made the long trip are now choosing the A-League instead.

"I think the establishment of the men's professional league in Australia [in 2004] is a reason for a lot of players to stay - they are quite happy to be professionals within their own country," Montemurro told BBC Sport.

"Also, there has been a lot of development in African and Asian countries which has likely widened the net of talent, which means clubs may look elsewhere."

Montemurro thinks the introduction of the WSL second division has probably helped more female Australian footballers play in England.

"The growth of the game in England in club professionalism and with the expansion of WSL to include a second tier [WSL 2] has contributed to more female Australians playing in England," he said.

There are four Australian players in WSL 2 - Alexia Apostolakis (Bristol City), Rachel Lowe (Durham), Kaitlyn Torpey (Newcastle) and Alana Murphy (Nottingham Forest).

Steph Catley, Kyra Cooney-Cross, Caitlin Foord (all Arsenal)

Emily van Egmond, Leah Davidson, Grace Johnston (all Charlton Athletic)

Holly McNamara, Clare Wheeler (both Everton)

Among Australia's men's squad, there are players spread across the world.

Four play in Australia's top flight, two play in the English Championship, three in Japan, and two each in Italy and Germany. The rest feature across countries including Scotland, Austria and the Netherlands.

The table below shows the Socceroos' dispersed overseas pathways.

Low salaries and competitive sporting landscape

The A-League Women (ALW), Australia's top-flight competition, was known as the W-League until 2021. Established in 2008, it initially appeared to be on an upward trajectory - with new clubs, leading Matildas and international players, growing crowds and increased media coverage.

But concerns have since emerged over its financial sustainability.

A 2025 players' union report , external found the ALW was "by far" Australia's lowest-paid professional women's competition. Minimum salaries were A$26,500 (about Â£13,900), compared with A$74,851 (Â£39,300) in women's cricket and A$67,337 (Â£35,400) in the AFL - the Australian rules competition.

The A-League Men and ALW are also the only major Australian sports competitions without a collective bargaining agreement, leaving the domestic game exposed to the threat of industrial action.

With average WSL salaries reported at about Â£47,000 in 2022 , the financial gap may well be a factor in why more female Australian players are choosing England.

Chelsea and Australia international Ellie Carpenter recently criticised , external the state of the Australian women's game after a pre-season friendly against Sydney FC.

"It's disappointing to see where the league is at here now in Australia, especially coming off the back of the World Cup in 2023 and the buzz here," Carpenter said.

"I really think that we need to follow that and we need to invest more."

Asked if she might return to play in Australia, Carpenter said finances would be a barrier.

"I don't think that's really on the cards, financially, for me to come back here," Carpenter said.

"Hopefully that changes and ending my career in Australia will be possible."

In 2025, Football Australia reported 1.93 million Australian participants , external , making it the country's most-played sport. Yet despite the Socceroos qualifying for six successive men's World Cups, Australia has no dedicated national headquarters for its teams, coaching programmes and administration.

The Home of the Matildas facility in Melbourne opened in 2023 but is not a permanent base for both senior national teams. The Socceroos continue to train at different venues depending on fixtures and availability.

That contrasts with nations such as England and France, which have dedicated centres at St George's Park and Clairefontaine.

Former Socceroos coach Graham Arnold described Football Australia as " homeless , external " in 2024 after his side prepared for World Cup qualifiers against Lebanon at the NSW Rugby League Centre of Excellence.

Montemurro believes Australia's size means more than one centre may be needed.

"We probably need one or two and we need some geographical touch points where we maybe have one where all the northern states can meet and then all the southern states can meet accordingly," he says.

"I think it would be important to have a couple of national centres where we can reconvene a lot of our development squads and our youth squads on a more regular basis.

"I believe a couple of base hubs in Australia could help our youth development."

Australia co-hosted the Women's World Cup in 2023, with the Matildas reaching the semi-finals for the first time after they beat France.

Their rise since then has turned them into one of Australia's most recognisable sporting brands, opening the door to opportunities overseas - evidence of the lasting impact that hosting a major tournament can have.

"The Women's World Cup in 2023 changed perception of the football landscape, not just the perception of the players but also the level of coaches, administrators and the general perception of football in Australia," Montemurro says.

articles.title: Columbia HSFB Team Snaps 101-Game Losing Streak, Longest in History, Led by Former NFL WR as HC
articles.summary: A losing streak that stretched to 101 games is finally over for Columbia High School in Huntsville, Alabama.
articles.body:
A losing streak that stretched to 101 games is finally over for Columbia High School in Huntsville, Alabama.

Columbia beat Greensboro High School 41-14 on Saturday.

"All the glory to God," Columbia coach Sammie Coates said, per AL.com's Thomas Ashworth . "God has blessed me to be in this situation to bring this to this school, to this community. I want to say thank you to the administration, to the school supporting me, having my back the whole time, and the players showing up and fighting every single day throughout the spring, throughout the summer, everything they have done.

"They deserve every moment of this. They stuck it out. Guys came out and helped support. We built the program, and it's coming. We ain't there yet, but we are coming."

Coates, who starred at Auburn as a wide receiver before playing four years in the NFL, is in his second season at the helm. According to Kaleigh Tingelstad and Mike Brown of 48 News in Huntsville, he had just 28 players on the roster by the time the 2025 campaign concluded.

Now, Columbia is 1-0 to kick off 2026, and the Eagles prevailed in emphatic fashion. They reeled off 41 unanswered points after going behind 14-0.

Running back Christian Richey was a standout performer, eclipsing 200 yards from scrimmage and scoring four touchdowns.

Having a coach with an NFL pedigree certainly helped to build Columbia's profile, and the school began working with Gatorade in August 2025 to give its players an added boost.

articles.title: The 2026 Fantasy Football Blueprint: Your guide to a championship is here
articles.summary: Your guide to a fantasy football championship in 2026 has arrived.
articles.body:
Fantasy football season is nearly upon us. In a matter of weeks, millions of people will draft their teams and begin the pursuit of fantasy glory. If we're being honest, millions of folks have already done just that.

For me, football is my year-round obsession. Not a day goes by that I don't consider the sport and the potential range of outcomes for the upcoming season. I think about this 365 days so you don't have to — I'm obsessed, so you get to enjoy your normal life. And I'm far from cursed in mine, to be fair.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Here, I'll lay out my blueprint for 2026 fantasy football drafts — a compilation of my thoughts about the game after charting hundreds of wide receiver routes, watching endless film and running through my projections for all 32 teams. I'll get some major assists along the way from the great folks I'm lucky to consider colleagues here at Yahoo. I'll point you to great work to read or listen to later and, hopefully, challenge the way you think.

If you're just now jumping back into football, welcome. If you've been keeping up with content all year, thank you for your support and for keeping the lights on. But the journey is just beginning for all of us.

So let's delay no further and unveil a blueprint to build your most successful season yet.

Jump to different destinations of the Blueprint with our table of contents:

If you know me, I am all about ecosystems. Fantasy football can be all about hammering players from the best ecosystems in the NFL. I always think back to the Peyton Manning- Broncos teams circa 2013. Sometimes winning your fantasy league is as simple as hoarding as many players from those kinds of special offenses.

It's obvious that great ecosystems equate to some of the most potent and efficient offenses in the NFL. They're surrounded by a quality line, loaded with good skill position talent and stewarded by a high-end play-caller. But there's more to it than that. It helps if you have concentrated target trees and clear backfield usage but you shouldn't just cross off teams that don't fit the bill. Ambiguous situations can still equal profit.

If anything, the lesson from last season was how much great play-callers and offensive designers matter. Teams like the Jaguars and Bears reached unseen heights with the additions of Liam Coen and Ben Johnson as play-calling head coaches. The Patriots got back on track with Josh McDaniels taking over the scoring unit. Even a team like New Orleans became the source of sneaky value down the stretch with Kellen Moore installing a progressive offense that ranked first in presnap motion. Most importantly, the teams that Johnson, Moore and Coen left behind in 2025 all experienced some regression offensively.

Players make the plays but great coaches lay the soil for those trees to grow.

NFL teams know the value of a great coach on offense, as over half the league turned over their play callers from 2025 to 2026. Everyone wants their version of Johnson, Coen or, in the most ideal world, Sean McVay, right now. With all the coaching turnover, I wrote up a piece back in February sorting the new hires into buckets based on how much I liked the move for fantasy football . Revisit that for the full analysis, but here, we will revisit the groupings ('I like it,' 'it's fine,' 'I'm skeptical') with some quick and updated thoughts on how those offenses project.

A hire that was met with skepticism, but frankly, I thought was a huge win; LaFleur is ready to at least be the architect of an offense. He was better than credited as the Jets' offensive coordinator, leaning into the right schematic buttons that boost modern offenses. I am Cardinals Curious and believe this team will be better offensively than the fantasy hivemind thinks, despite long-term quarterback questions.

Ravens hire HC Jesse Minter, OC Declan Doyle will call plays

Doyle is a young and intriguing hire off the Sean Payton and Ben Johnson coaching tree. We are likely to see something similar to what the Bears ran in 2025. Expect plenty of zone rushing and play action on downfield route concepts.

The Bills promoting Brady likely keeps more of the same in place with the Bills. I'm higher on Brady than most in the space. Many of the outside complaints about Brady's offense — heavy use of mesh, tons of screens/short throws and a tendency to go run-heavy — are mostly forced into the unit because of personnel problems. I expect the addition of DJ Moore and perhaps getting the running backs more involved in the passing game, as has been reported from camp, will solve a lot of that.

It may not all come together for fantasy football in 2026 but this was a great hire. Kubiak did almost everything you want out of a modern offensive coordinator last season. Seattle made use of heavy personnel packages to increase the efficiency of the passing game, ran under-center play action and was fifth in dropback motion rate. He's also not a one-hit wonder, as he was doing most of this for a 2024 Saints team that had its moments offensively but fell apart due to injuries. Let's just hope Ashton Jeanty will be on the field to reap the benefits of this new system.

Just like everyone else, I'm excited about the idea of adding Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator to an already strong team under Jim Harbaugh and a talented offense. If you're interested in chasing the hype, however, expect to pay a heavy ADP price. The pursuit may well be worth it. We've never seen McDaniel's offense operated by a quarterback as talented as Justin Herbert and this team is quietly loaded at all skill position spots. Unfortunately, the offensive line is dealing with injuries yet again.

Falcons hire HC Kevin Stefanski, OC Tommy Rees will call plays

I'll admit I'm mixed on this one and the quarterback situation makes it even murkier. However, I think Stefanski is a quality offensive coach and his scheme does fit with Atlanta 's talent. He's a sensible option but might not be a true needle-mover like some of these other names. Rees is also an unproven variable and I wouldn't say anything from recent Browns seasons push my opinion one way or another.

Blough coached under Kingsbury the last two seasons but I expect he will present a somewhat left-turn schematically from the spread tenets of that offense. Blough began his career in 2019 with the Detroit Lions as a backup quarterback and hung onto the roster through Ben Johnson's rise up the ranks from offensive quality control coach, tight ends coach and ultimately to a passing game coordinator role in 2021, where, after Anthony Lynn was demoted, he helped head coach Dan Campbell bring to life what we now identify as the Lions offense. Blough would return to Detroit in one of Johnson's final seasons with the club as the offensive coordinator when he was no doubt already eyeing a move to the coaching ranks. My suspicion was that Blough probably leans more toward the ideas of Johnson's scheme.

Monken has head coaching experience at Southern Mississippi from 2013 to 2015 and has most recently been the architect of a Ravens offense that ranked third in EPA per play and fourth in success rate since his arrival in 2023. While Lamar Jackson deserves a good chunk of that credit, there's no doubt that Monken helped evolve the MVP quarterback's game. His presence with this team makes me more optimistic when selecting the pass-catchers despite obvious quarterback questions surrounding named-starter Deshaun Watson and big-name backup Shedeur Sanders .

The Lions picking Drew Petzing for the offensive coordinator job got flamed on the internet but just as the section implies, I thought the hire was … just fine. To be clear, there are some justifiable critiques of his play-calling work and pre-snap alignment of Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson with the Cardinals, and those are areas where the 38-year-old needs to improve. However, my hunch is he's mostly in Detroit to revive its run game, which stalled out last year under John Morton, while the passing game principles held by Dan Campbell will remain the same.

Slowik became a bit of a punching bag by the end of his watch as the Texans offensive coordinator in 2024 but I think he's worth a second look at the position. Slowik couldn't evolve the offense as the team had hoped from the "The Shanahan Greatest Hits" compilation they ran in 2023 to a more three-receiver spread unit in 2024. However, he did good work in that first year and was on this Dolphins staff last season. I can't imagine he's going to come in here and tear down a successful run game, which matters for De'Von Achane, the only Miami player drafted highly in fantasy.

Two noteworthy takeaways come from Seattle's hiring of Brian Fleury. For starters, it's interesting that Seattle, which had some internal candidates to replace Klint Kubiak, decided to go outside the building and pluck another Shanahan tree member. The second is that Fleury, who was most recently the tight ends coach in San Francisco since 2022 and held the title of run game coordinator last year, has an extremely varied background. My hunch is that Seattle won't change much of its stripes, but will hope Fleury can keep beefing up the run game — good news for Jadarian Price.

You can think what you want about Robinson's overall offensive attack in Atlanta. It wasn't perfect. However, he was objectively good for receiver usage, most notably when his motion concepts allowed all four of the main pass-catchers to get a 39% or higher slot rate on passing downs in 2024. This usage awaits for Emeka Egbuka , someone I'm drafting with a ton of confidence if healthy.

Brian Daboll has quarterback-development skins on the wall he can point to during his recent stints with the Bills and Giants. However, you can also argue that the Bills got better offensively when they moved away from his heavy spread concepts after he departed and Daniel Jones played his best football in a much better-designed unit last year with the Colts . My quick take on Daboll is that he helps get your quarterback on base but his spread-and-shred stylings lead to way too much long-term volatility. For Tennessee and Cam Ward , getting on base would be progress.

Broncos promote OC Davis Webb , give him play-calling duties

The Broncos clearly felt the heat from what was a relatively hot cycle of interest in their 31-year-old former quarterback coach, Davis Webb. From what I hear, Webb and Bo Nix have a tight connection and this move likely signals their desire to help the young passer take the next step. That should be doable in 2026, especially with Jaylen Waddle in tow. I do wonder if Sean Payton doesn't get back in the play-calling chair at some point if this gets off to a slow start.

I like the idea of Mannion bringing in some tenets from Green Bay and that offensive family. It can help smooth out some of the rough edges in Philly's passing game from last year. But it's a big change for the Eagles based on how they've played under Jalen Hurts . It will be a lot to oversee for the 33-year-old riser, who was on NFL rosters as a player as recently as 2023 and spent the last two years with the Packers as an offensive assistant and then quarterback coach.

Giants hire HC John Harbaugh, OC Matt Nagy will call plays

The Chiefs essentially fired Matt Nagy. They can try to soften and launder it through the media but they let him walk out the door without a thought to keeping him before he took a coordinator job in February, only after the Giants didn't land Monken. That's a firing and based on how it went in Kansas City , I don't blame them for wanting to make a change. I also find the fit with Jaxson Dart a little odd.

I don't think Mike McCarthy is some miserable hire by the Steelers, but I think we can agree it was uninspiring and likely doesn't push them out of the stagnation that befell them during the late Tomlin years. I have two major hang-ups about McCarthy as the offensive architect in Pittsburgh . For starters, it's tough that this is being framed as a way to make Aaron Rodgers , who was a bottom-tier quarterback last year, more comfortable. Second, it's hard not to notice that the Packers and even the 2025 Cowboys immediately got better right after McCarthy left, as a younger play-caller took over and installed a more dynamic offense with under-center concepts and more motion.

At least we have a clear idea of what the attack will look like under McCarthy. He'll cede plenty of pre-snap control to Rodgers and likely run an old West Coast offense out of mostly 11 personnel. Expect a lot of quick game to Michael Pittman Jr. and the occasional boundary shot to DK Metcalf .

Honestly, I didn't get this one. Tanner Engstrand designed a good passing game but the sequencing and rushing attack in 2025 wasn't ideal. If you want to start over, that's fine but I'm not sure Reich, who felt out of step with the league in his static RPO-heavy offense with the Panthers before a midseason firing in 2023, is the answer. The Jets quietly have a good group of weapons but color me skeptical this will be what unlocks them.

Whether analysts know it or want to admit it, best ball brain has seeped into all of our content. The popularity and fun of the format have made it hard to transition the way we talk about that game into traditional redraft leagues.

Straight up, there is a massive difference.

With everyone obsessed with taking down these massive best-ball contests, we've gotten overly obsessed with the end of the season. You'll hear folks say "Weeks 15, 16, 17 …the ones that matter most for fantasy football" when analyzing individual player or team outlooks. No one is denying that those weeks are huge even for managed teams. Those are the fantasy football playoffs and we all want to win those weeks to take the league championship. Yet, what goes under-discussed is that you have to get there in the first place for them to matter at all.

Back when I was oh so young and carefree, I was always so concerned with exposing myself to late-year upside. My brain was dialed in on the hot finish, never concerning myself with the beginning of the race. I'd figure it out somewhere along the way; August drafts were the concern, not the starting roster of "September me."

No one has caused me to reevaluate that stance more than Scott Pianowski. He wrote about the benefits of starting fast and has pushed our Yahoo Fantasy Forecast listeners to draft to "win September." I repeat it all the time now; he's won the war on the hot start and drilled it into my brain.

Best of all? The numbers are on his side.

Last season, 90.9% of fantasy managers who started off 5-0 made the playoffs. That didn't automatically land you a championship but almost a quarter of them (24.5%) did win their leagues. This has been consistent every single season I've looked into this data. As is what happens when you start 3-2, where it could go either way; it hovers around 50% of those teams making the playoffs.

It's never been more apparent that life is just a lot easier if you're riding hot coming into mid-October. You can start stacking your bench with late-season upside stashes like your favorite rookie receiver or a high-end backup running back when you don't have to worry about chasing needs on waivers. You can get the best of both worlds with that hot start.

We all want to make it to the end of the season but you need to win early to clear the path. Just don't get caught looking forward to the destination and forget to focus on simply merging onto the freeway.

How can we start off our leagues on the right note? Avoid the allure and delayed gratification siren song of the suspended replacement-level receiver or injury discount. Break ties in favor of players in proven situations with projectable volume. Thankfully, the great Justin Boone is in house to help us with early-season strength of schedule projections . These aren't everything and Boone would tell you that. However, again, it allows us to break ties.

We here at Yahoo Fantasy implore you to Win September. Once you do, everything will get easier as you march on toward the weeks that matter most.

Fantasy analysts spend most of the pre-draft process in the summer talking about breakouts and sleepers but we tend to never investigate the first-round picks. Yet, if your first-round selection flops, your season isn't over, but it sure does start off behind the eight-ball. As such, I wanted to dedicate some space here to diving into the consensus top picks in Yahoo ADP and discussing any reservations I have with each player, even if I am generally in on all these guys. You can decide for yourself if any of these variables presented are enough to dock a player outside of Round 1 for someone else — those options will be presented after.

It's nearly impossible to make a negative argument on this one. Gibbs is an explosive, young and ascending running back tied to a great offensive environment. He's been hit-or-miss in pass protection and could lose reps there — I just don't know who the Lions would be putting on the field over him. Detroit did lose its free-agent center addition Cade Mays for an extended stretch and he was meant to beef up the interior.

Robinson has lost goal-line work in previous years and Brian Robinson Jr. is now in the mix to replace Tyler Allgeier as the backup. The Falcons' offensive line has some holes and they don't project to be a strong offense regardless of whether Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. starts more games.

The most difficult of the top-five to paint a negative case of, outside of "His quarterback could get hurt." Even then, Chase averages 2.12 yards per route run (557 routes) since 2023 when Joe Burrow isn't on the field.

There's a chance Nacua doesn't play in Week 1 with league discipline for off-field missteps hanging over his head. And while Matthew Stafford stayed healthy all last season, you'd be foolish to assume that's definitely happening in 2026 after the reports from August 2025. Nacua is also an injury risk himself.

The 49ers star was the best player in fantasy last season. He's done it before and the next seasons … haven't been the best rides. It's concerning that he's coming off a season with an unprecedented workload, even for him.

If he wears down, you can't say you couldn't see it coming.

The reigning Offensive Player of the Year had a 35.8% target share of the Seahawks offense, the highest for any receiver the last 10 seasons. You have to imagine some regression in that consolidation, as well as his efficiency downfield.

All of the Colts were hit hard when the offense fell apart after Daniel Jones' first injury but Taylor was impacted most of all. He didn't clear 16 fantasy points in any game from Week 12 on. His 83 receptions are outside of the top 30 at the position since 2023, trailing Joe Mixon, who didn't play a down of football last year.

Honestly, really difficult to come up with a negative for St. Brown — he's not the first receiver I'd ask to run a go route from the X-receiver spot but that doesn't matter for fantasy football. Since 2022, when he became a full-time starter, he ranks first in catches (457), fourth in yards (5,340), third in touchdowns (39) and third in first downs per route run. I'm not sure what's stopping this train. I have St. Brown ranked ahead of Smith-Njigba for this season.

You always have to worry about Josh Allen stealing touchdowns. Cook's average 8.7% target share ranks 25th among running backs in the last three seasons. I have some hope that the second variable changes in 2026 but it's a projection.

I have Lamb in the same tier as his teammate, George Pickens, at wide receiver. So it's pretty live odds to me that the latter outscores the former. The Cowboys offense should be good enough for everyone to get home, and Lamb was slightly more productive than Pickens in the games they both played last season. It was still tight enough to make some nervous about spending a Round 1 selection.

Look no further than what happened last year when Jefferson finished as the WR37 in per-game scoring. Now, with Kyler Murray likely starting most of the season, it should be better. However, Murray is a flawed quarterback who doesn't fit the offense perfectly. There's a chance he's not under center by the fantasy playoffs.

Look no further than what happened last year, when Jeanty finished as the RB17 in per-game scoring. Much of that wasn't Jeanty's fault — the ecosystem around him was bad. I'm trusting its better this season but we're drafting him with the assumption it will be sizably better. Expect his injury to push him out of the first round in ADP. Speaking of which …

Names you should consider if picks 10-12 bother you

The Eagles offense went stagnant last season but I'm not sure that I saw any dip in Barkley's individual play. The offensive line should be healthier this year and if Sean Mannion is a hit as the play-caller, the unit will be more efficient overall. I like betting on one last big year from Barkley.

Speaking of seeing no dip in play, Derrick Henry averaged more yards after contact (3.59 to 3.5) in 2025 than 2024. There are zero signs of decline when watching Henry. So, while he is well into an outlier zone from an age standpoint, I will not be the first off the ship. The Ravens didn't grab any real competition for the future Hall of Famer, who basically walks into the season with 10-plus touchdowns in his back pocket.

A proven explosive-play specialist meets a team in desperate need for his skills. Over the last two seasons combined, the Kansas City Chiefs rank dead last with a 2.9% explosive rushing rate on running back runs. The teams ranked just ahead of them, the Browns and Raiders, both hover around 5.3%. Walker is going to be a massive changing force for the Chiefs — he's a viable 12th overall pick. He is going too early to place him in the section you'll read below later, but he is a "My Guy" type of pick for me in 2026.

The Texans wideout is one of the best players at his position since 2023. His only question is availability.

Before you comment about his quarterback, who was terrible in the postseason (Collins didn't play, which matters), Collins did the vast majority of that damage with C.J. Stroud under center. Collins has WR1 upside if he stays healthy and the offense stabilizes under Nick Caley in Year 2.

One of the biggest mistakes fantasy football players make is that they're too quick to write off possible rebound seasons. "That guy burned me and I'll never take him again" is an emotional response and leads to missed opportunities.

If the circumstances are different, we should be willing to imagine new results. Players are not numbers on a spreadsheet and the NFL is an ever-changing league. In a small-sample-size game like football where the landscape changes, it's borderline insane to write these types of post-hype sleeper cases off.

I wrote up 10 disappointing picks from 2025 who need a reboot this season . I'm not drafting all of them but I'm not closed off to them, either. Diving into those cases at least provides us with a path for attacking possible rebounds.

The quick and easy rule that I tend to follow is this: if a player is in their prime years and not coming back from a significant injury and is a proven good talent — AKA, look at something beyond the fantasy points — you should almost never put that guy on your "do not draft" list. Fortune favors the open-minded.

Another Scott Pianowski gem that's become a hard and fast truth for me as I've gotten older: "Injuries will find your fantasy team during the season, you don't have to go looking for them in the draft."

It's always tempting to look at a name you know and a player who, at their best, can outproduce many of the names close to them on the draft board. You want to stick them on your bench, wait it out and imagine a powerhouse starting lineup when they're back in some far-off, distant Week 6 fantasy world. You think you're getting a discount but, because you have absolutely no idea when that "at their best" will arrive, oftentimes you're just catching the falling knife.

Living by this rule has been a pretty dogmatic approach of mine the last few years. Avoiding the landmines has been quite profitable.

However, as with all principles, you have to know when to make exceptions. That's why this year, in this section, I want to talk about a player you should consider an exception: Malik Nabers .

Back in July, I planned to list Nabers as a full fade. The tenor around his cleanup surgery, rehab and overall status returning from an ACL tear was incredibly negative. Every beat writer report was a black cloud, all comments from head coach John Harbaugh shrouded in darkness. And yet, he came out in training camp and participated in individual drills with few limitations as a route runner. As of late, he's been ramping up toward team drills.

If you experienced whiplash from the reports, you weren't alone. Yet, as we stand here in August, we're in a much better place with Nabers. As a reminder, when Nabers got hurt last season, he was tracking toward becoming a true Tier 1 receiver in the NFL — a designation I don't use lightly.

I think expecting Nabers to be at his best would be foolish. Yet, I'm comfortable with grabbing a lesser version of a guy knocking on the door to being elite in early Round 3. Right now, I have Nabers ranked inside my top-30 overall players. He's someone I'm willing to make an exception for as a funnel target who is a freak athletic mover. Even if fully healthy, we would have some questions about his offensive environment, but even those wouldn't be serious enough to bump him outside the top two rounds.

So, I'm comfortable with the discount here to grab a guy more talented with access to more targets than the other wideouts who go in his range.

In past sections of this piece, I've advocated for swimming into the current of the top-tier quarterbacks and snagging the raw point advantage this year. Those players, especially consensus QB1 overall, Josh Allen, still possess that same ceiling. However, one thing that I think fantasy gamers don't remember is that your strategy at one position must incorporate your approach to all others. With that in mind, Late Round QB is absolutely back on the menu for 2026.

The strategy never truly left us but I believe it's almost without a doubt the best way to construct rosters. The strength of other positions, plus a flat Tier 3 of quarterbacks that goes from around QB7 to 16 or 17 depending on your preferences, has me waiting until Round 9 or later to grab a passer.

The biggest variable here is that I believe falling behind at running back is something you simply can't afford in 2026. At the same time, I want to make sure my receiver spots are covered with a pair of high-end target-getters after WR2 scoring took a nosedive in 2025. As such, it's nearly impossible to afford shopping in the elite aisle at both of the onesie positions in fantasy. A quick look at the quality depth between both tight end and quarterback makes the decision easier.

All of my least favorite drafts have come when I make exceptions for a high-end passer who fell a little bit beyond ADP. I suspect I'll keep dropping quarterbacks down my overall rankings every time I go in for an update.

My third tier of quarterback begins at Trevor Lawrence and Justin Herbert, two of my favorite grabs if I'm going "early." Yet, I can kick the can down to a Jared Goff and Malik Willis tandem in the double-digit rounds and feel quite set at quarterback.

As mentioned above, you can't fall behind at running back this year. The best way to know if you have done just that: you enter Round 5 without an RB2 and are staring down the Quinshon Judkins, Bucky Irving, TreVeyon Henderson grouping between picks 50 to 65. There are some players in this bucket I like and am actively targeting — not Henderson at ADP — but they profile more as strong flex options and far too volatile RB2s.

Based on all the exercises I've done so far, I prefer to leave my drafts with two running backs in the first four rounds.

Obviously, in Round 1 you are generally at the mercy of where you end up picking. If you end up in the third spot, you should turn the card in for Ja'Marr Chase. However, I've consistently found myself moving the second tier of running backs up my overall rankings as we get further into August. As it stands, I have nine running backs in my top-15 overall rankings and 11 in the top 19. Picks 30 to 42 also include five more.

For the most part, all of my top 18 running backs this year are players who have a clear-cut case to be, if not the workhorse back, the obvious leading man in their backfields. You want a strong foundation of those players as teams lean into heavier formations and beef up their ground game to stay efficient on offense against modern coverages. There are running backs available late who can make be a part of that boom as well but with so many quality options available at the top, and the depth at receiver, I know which position I'm not eschewing early.

Your approach to fantasy football drafting should always mirror where the league is heading from a macro perspective. The league-wide rushing rate on early downs was 49% last season. That's up from 48.4% in 2024 and 47.7% in 2023. From 2018 to 2020, you're looking at 46.3%. Sensing the theme here?

Teams have reinvested in their rushing ecosystems to regain the upper hand on defenses. Shift your draft approach accordingly.

We remain in a golden age for wide receiver play in the NFL. I can go all the way down to the 40s in my "real-life" wide receiver rankings before I land on a player whom I think has legitimate question marks about whether they can be a bona fide starting wide receiver and a top-two option on a team. It's just one example, but my ranking of the top-15 wide receivers 25 and under helps show why this position gets better every year .

All that said, one of the themes of the 2025 season was that WR2 scoring was down relative to recent history.

While it may seem like that reality and the concept of the position being deeper than ever are incongruous, they aren't. The fact that there are more good receivers than ever has forced teams into rotations at the position in some extreme circumstances. Even more critical, we saw teams move toward heavy personnel packages with multiple tight ends on the field, taking one wide receiver off the field. I had a long conversation with JJ Zachariason about this earlier in the offseason:

Taking a receiver off the field and adding a heavier body — whether it's a tight end or fullback — only pushes the target consolidation more toward the WR1 in an offense. The Seahawks were one of the teams that skewed heavier last season and we saw Jaxon Smith-Njigba own the highest target share for a wide receiver since 2015. That's the trend, not the exception, as teams get into those looks.

With that in mind, despite loving the depth options this year, I think you want to secure a pair of strong wide receiver starters in the first five rounds this year. The first two rounds have plenty of strong options.

However, this all comes to focus once you get into Rounds 4 to the mid-sixth range. That area of the draft this year is absolutely loaded with breakout receivers, guys on the rise and a handful of older veterans still getting it done. The depth of the position league-wide is best felt in this range.

Grab several, then wait to attack it again when the position beefs up in Round 9. Even in that range between picks 90 and 120, you'll find so many good bets.

The clear need to prioritize running backs and receivers in the first five rounds is why I'm punting off quarterback. However, the other onesie position does make a strong claim to be in the mix.

My approach to tight ends this year is similar but less strict than my quarterback plan. The top two of Brock Bowers and Trey McBride just don't find their way onto my rosters much because they will damage the path to clarity at running back and/or receiver. If I'm picking one at ADP, it will be Bowers as McBride is a clear regression candidate after running a league-high 691 routes in 2025.

I am doing most of my shopping in the fourth to sixth round. For starters, Colston Loveland in the fourth round is a pick I've made several times. He belongs in the Bowers and McBride tier. When everyone was available in the playoffs, Loveland led the Bears with a 79% route participation and 28% target share. He's an excellent football player and perfectly weaponized in this system.

There is a tier drop down to Tyler Warren, Sam LaPorta and Tucker Kraft but I find all of those guys to be strong picks. LaPorta is the one I've taken most, just relative to ADP in the 60s. The next grouping includes Kyle Pitts Sr. and Harold Fannin Jr.; I'm more interested in the latter.

Regardless of your favorite name here, I don't want to wait later than this. It gets tricky in a hurry.

Anyone with experience playing fantasy football knows that rookies can make your fantasy season. We don't quite have the high-caliber prospects we're used to in this class, especially at running back. Nevertheless, there are still a good crop of guys in the rookie class who will be main characters of the fantasy season, and perhaps a back-half of the season breakout. Here, I'll introduce you to every rookie selected on Day 1 and 2 of the 2026 NFL Draft.

The first overall pick won't start the season as QB1, barring some major change in the Raiders' plans. The Las Vegas braintrust wants to start Kirk Cousins and allow Mendoza to develop. We'll see him at some point this season and I have faith he's good enough of a prospect to be an answer for the Raiders in time, and for Brock Bowers right away.

If we get a Ty Simpson start this season, something has gone terribly wrong in Los Angeles. The Rams don't even have Simpson working as the backup in camp. He is, hopefully, their long-term answer but is merely a developmental body in 2026.

The Cardinals took Beck in Round 3 to provide youth and some competition behind Jacoby Brissett. There's a real chance we see Beck down the stretch of 2026, but Brissett would likely have to play his way out of the job.

The Steelers snagged Allar as a developmental body in Round 3. He has plenty of tools but just never strung them all together. He's a longshot to see the field in 2026.

Love is an explosive three-down threat as a running back. He can make big plays on the ground and brings verifiable receiving chops. He's a third-round pick in redraft leagues but comes with a little more risk now that he suffered a high ankle sprain in the preseason. The good news is that he was operating as the clear lead back before the injury, not in a timeshare. Once he's healthy in October or so, he has the upside to be a true RB1 out the gate if the Cardinals offense is better than most expect — I'm high on what they can be from a structural perspective.

The Seahawks tried to trade out of the 32nd overall pick but ultimately stood pat and selected Price. He's walking into this team as Kenneth Walker III's direct replacement. We could see Price in something of a timeshare but he will get enough base-down work for a team that wants to rely on its ground game to justify his mid-round ADP.

The latest 49ers' mid-round running back gambit, Black has a shot to be the direct backup to Christian McCaffrey but nothing more than that. You need to track this depth chart behind McCaffrey in August to maybe know for sure.

One Day 3 sleeper for the road: Jonah Coleman, Broncos

A reliable, rugged runner who doesn't fumble, drop passes and holds up in pass protection; you can see why Sean Payton liked this guy as a prospect. Coleman has a chance to earn a rotational role early on in his career and could be the guy who inherits the most base-down work if J.K. Dobbins gets hurt. RJ Harvey didn't shine in that regard last season.

The Titans aggressively took Tate at fourth overall but he gives them a man-beating perimeter presence they simply didn't have on the roster. He is a WR3 candidate for fantasy this season as he's going to be in a high-degree-of-difficulty X-receiver role with a young quarterback still finding his way. However, if Cam Ward hits, his game overlaps well with Tate on vertical targets outside the numbers.

Tyson was one of the best zone-beaters in the last few draft classes among prospects I charted, and he landed in New Orleans, where he'll move across the formation and get favorable matchups alongside a WR1 in Chris Olave. The Saints offense is on the rise and Tyson will go with it, when he's healthy later on in the season.

The last word is quite heavy in this instance. Tyson was dogged by injuries throughout his college career, including a hamstring that cut his 2025 season short. That same injury kept him from participating in predraft testing, held him out of portions of the Saints' offseason practices and he's now dealing with yet another hamstring issue that will almost certainly cause him to miss games to start his rookie season. That makes him an incredibly risky click and I had to dock him outside the top 90 selections, but he still presents a high-ceiling dart throw.

The Round 1 rookie is a good dynasty stash and may well come on late in the season. However, he is likely a slow start candidate with a limited role. He's missed a ton of time with a hamstring injury this offseason and was only ever going to top out as the WR2 across from DeVonta Smith. My guess is Dontayvion Wicks opens up the season as that player now.

KC Concepcion was my WR2 in this year's draft and is an explosive separator who can win with the ball in his hands. There are obvious quarterback questions in Cleveland but if Concepcion gets the short-area layup role, he could offset that. I just think the talent is well worth the risk at an ADP outside the top-120 picks for such a talented player.

Cooper is a slot-based receiver who is tough as any prospect you'll see coming into the league. He has strong hands and is tough to tackle in open space. He can be incredibly useful to the Jets offense but he would need to unseat AD Mitchell for outside receiver snaps to get enough playing time to even be on the fantasy radar.

I know that Stribling was panned as the 33rd overall pick, but I thought he was a viable Day 2 prospect — obviously that was as early as it gets on Day 2. He fits the 49ers offense quite well as an inside/outside power player who flashed some promising release moves. With Ricky Pearsall out for the season, Stribling started off as a late-round sleeper in all formats, but he's moved well beyond that with his performance in preseason games .

I thought Boston should have been a Round 1 pick and is a better separator than credited for a big wideout. One of the consistent drumbeats out of Cleveland this offseason is that Boston has looked excellent. He's started to get reps with the first team as the X-receiver. Long term, Boston and Concepcion are going to be an excellent tandem. For fantasy this year, if Boston can push aside Jerry Jeudy — quite possible — he will at least be a volatile bye week filler.
