articles.title: Premier League season predictions: Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville pick the title winner and players to watch in 2026/27
articles.summary: Arsenal tipped to defend their Premier League crown but opinion is split on the race for Europe, relegation and players and managers to watch as Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville make their predictions...
articles.body:
Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville made their 2026/27 Premier League season predictions on Monday Night Football.

Title winners

Jamie Carragher - Arsenal

A few weeks ago, I thought Man City might have a chance - but it was all around Rodri. If Rodri stayed I'd maybe make a case for them, but without Rodri, I just can't see it.

Gary Neville - Arsenal

One hundred per cent Arsenal. They're way out in front. With what they've got already now in defence and in midfield, with the good attackers that they've got, they've got a really good standard, then they're fine.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Latest on YOUR PL club!
  • Premier League fixtures & scores | FREE PL highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Top-four finishers

Jamie Carragher - Man City, Chelsea, Liverpool

Man City are better than Chelsea but the European factor can play a huge part. We saw Manchester United last season. It gives them a big lift, Chelsea.

I think Liverpool would want more, but I think just looking at the Chelsea situation, Liverpool where they are right now, I don't see any way they'd be in the top two, and I don't see any way they can mount a title challenge.

Gary Neville - Chelsea, Man City, Man Utd

Chelsea second? Just purely because of the fact that they've got no European football. If they keep Enzo Fernandez, with Moises Caicedo in midfield, with that front three, and they're only playing 45 games, they're going to amass an enormous amount of points.

That's based upon the fact that they're going to have more free weeks, they're not going to have the injury pressures, they're not going to have the travelling that comes with European football, and the mental fatigue that comes with that. I think they'll just edge past Manchester City.

I can't separate Man Utd and Liverpool in fourth place, I genuinely have no idea. I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth.

Fifth and sixth?

Jamie Carragher - Man Utd, Spurs

Gary Neville - Liverpool, Brighton

Sometimes you look at Spurs going, 'oh, they've spent a lot of money' and thinking 'quite exciting for Spurs fans, they're finally splashing the cash'. But then I look at the team and I think, 'where's it all gone?'

Savinho and Omar Marmoush will make them a lot better, but I just don't know whether they'll pull it together and that's the question.

I know Brighton are a good unit, they're reliable, they're consistent and I think Brentford and Brighton, those two teams this season may just get in there because they're consistent and they know what they're doing and they're well-drilled.

A well-organised, well-drilled team will beat a team of talented players who are still trying to find their way.

European contender?

Jamie Carragher - Brentford

A lot of people say, when you're managing a club like Brentford, which is so well-run behind the scenes and the hierarchy, it makes it easier for the manager. Of course it does - but watching them this weekend, watching them last season...

Brentford haven't got European football, so I think that will be a big plus for them. I really love watching Brentford play, and for me, that was the best performance of the week [their win over Spurs].

Gary Neville - Spurs

Relegated

Jamie Carragher - Ipswich, Hull, Sunderland

Why Sunderland? The fact that they've got European football, they're going to be doing a lot of Thursday-Sunday. I think Sunderland last season reminded me a little bit of Sheffield United under Chris Wilder, where they came up and had a really brilliant season, finished high up the table but a lot of the games, like Sunderland, you win by the odd goal.

I'm not saying it's luck but their underlying numbers had them not far away from relegation.

Gary Neville - Coventry, Hull, Ipswich

I hope that one or two of the promoted sides stay up but I've not got the faith I had last season.

Having watched what I've seen this weekend, I'm going to go for the three promoted teams to go down.

Relegation risk

Jamie Carragher - Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace haven't had a great pre-season. They lost the first game at Everton, which, to be fair, they were actually very unlucky when you look at the chances they had. I know they had Europe last season, but a new manager, new in the Premier League, lost a few players, still in Europe... I'd probably go Crystal Palace to have a scare.

Gary Neville - Fulham

Watching Fulham [against Chelsea], that's a risk, that's a big risk. Young players, splitting your centre-backs like that, being open...

Top scorer

Jamie Carragher - Erling Haaland

Gary Neville - Erling Haaland

Impact signing

Jamie Carragher - Mateus Fernandes, Spurs

I really liked Mateus Fernandes last season at West Ham and I thought there might be another few teams in for him, better teams than Spurs.

Gary Neville - Bruno Guimaraes, Arsenal

He's the best signing by a mile.

If you take a player out of Arsenal's team anywhere, probably David Raya is the other one, but in the outfield parts of the pitch, there isn't a drop-off between the first and second choice anywhere, apart from Declan Rice. There's a massive drop when Declan Rice moves out of the team. If Rice gets injured for three months, that would be a risk to Arsenal.

The signing of [Bruno Guimaraes] removes that risk.

He is a massive personality. A different player than Rice but you talk about personality and character on the pitch... he is a brilliant personality. He believes he can win every single football match for his team. He believes he can tackle, he's aggressive, he's somebody you'd want alongside you...And by the way, £75m compared to some of the others that have gone for more is value in this market.

Player to watch

Jamie Carragher - Jeremy Jacquet, Liverpool

He's played one Premier League game and he's only played one pre-season game for Liverpool. [Jeremy Jacquet] looked really good in both games but you know sometimes when you look at a player and they just look the part.

I think this is the first season where a player alongside Virgil van Dijk is going to have to play his own game and at times look after Van Dijk.

Gary Neville - Morgan Rogers, Chelsea

When you're a £120m player you've got to hit numbers. You've got to be 12, 15 goals, you've got to be 10, 12 assists or else you're going to come under pressure.

We know he's a good player, Morgan Rogers. We'd all like him at our clubs. But £120m? Wow.

If he can deliver this season for Chelsea they can go and push Arsenal.

Manager to watch

Jamie Carragher - Matthias Jaissle, Newcastle

He's only young but he's got that little twinkle in his eye. I think Matthias Jaissle will be a fiery character in the Premier League. He's coming to Newcastle, a huge football club, and put in that performance [on Sunday]. I think he's got something about him.

Gary Neville - Xabi Alonso, Chelsea

If he gets the recruitment right and he keeps the players in those front areas of the pitch and he sorts the defence and the goalkeeper out he could be the emerging manager - out of that five that are below Mikel Arteta that are trying to win the league - he could be the next one to win the league

I think this season is critical for him because he's got to finish second or a good third because if he doesn't, without European football, with that squad that he's amassed, then there would be questions.

He's the manager of Chelsea - that means that he basically makes the final decision on transfers, on recruitment. If he goes and does one or two pieces of business in this next week or so, he's got to look after himself and demand that he gets that one or two players in this next week and we know where those areas are.

articles.title: SEC Issues Statement Opposing NFL Players Returning to CFB amid Latest Commits to Lane Kiffin, LSU
articles.summary: With eligibility controversies surrounding LSU and the SEC ahead of the 2026 season, the conference released a statement Monday saying it opposes NFL players returning to the college ranks.
articles.body:
With eligibility controversies surrounding LSU and the SEC ahead of the 2026 season, the conference released a statement Monday saying it opposes NFL players returning to the college ranks.

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference," the statement said. "Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition.

"Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes.

"College sports are for college athletes. The current confusion around national eligibility standards emphasizes the need to advance the Protect College Sports Act."

This comes as LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin appear primed to add a handful of players who seemed to be done at the collegiate level.

ESPN's Max Olson noted former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Wright plans to join the Tigers after he clears waivers in the NFL following the Cleveland Browns' decision to waive him. What's more, former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris is also committed to LSU after the New Orleans Saints waived him earlier this month.

Former Notre Dame defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka also committed to LSU.

Olson reported those are three of the 16 players who are now eligible for a fifth year after a Louisiana court granted them a temporary restraining order.

"At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they're either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country," Kiffin told reporters Monday. "So we've made the decision to recruit them like probably most people are."

It is another step in his aggressive roster-building strategy ahead of what will be his first season at LSU.

He also landed the top-ranked 2026 transfer portal class, per 247Sports , and seems set to add more talent that was competing for NFL roster spots not long ago.

articles.title: Durand Cup triumph a whiff of redemption for Edmund and Habas
articles.summary: Football News: KOLKATA: When peopleâs paths cross, sometimes it comes with the whiff of a road movie evolving and eventually moving their journey towards its point o.
articles.body: KOLKATA: When peopleâs paths cross, sometimes it comes with the whiff of a road movie evolving and eventually moving their journey towards its point of redemption with a profound sense of inevitability.For Edmund Lalrindika and Antonio Lopez Habas â the two main characters of East Bengal FCâs audacious dismantling of Mohun Bagan SG on their way to winning the Durand Cup here on Sunday, their journeys perhaps wield a symbolism with much depth and emotional nuance. They are about returning to the battle front not only to survive a seemingly insurmountable ordeal but completing an unfinished business with a beguiling element of defiance.Six years ago it was at the very Salt Lake Stadium, Edmund saw his journey suffer an unexpected setback. Five days after joining an Alejandro Menendezâs East Bengal on a short-term loan deal from Bengaluru FC, the Mizo youngster made debut in the first-leg I-League derby in the 2019-2020 season, coming off the bench to provide an assist for Macros Jimenezâs goal in a match which Mohun Bagan eventually won 2-1. It was the penultimate I-League derby between the two traditional rivals before their foray into the Indian Super League which was coronated as the countryâs top-tier league. Edmundâs stay in the match was merely 14-minute long as it was cut short with a serious injury, forcing him to leave the field and return to the BFC fold.Two years later, another spine injury put a serious question mark over his future, with his doctors having advised to stay away from football. But Edmund defied the odds with his customary grit and a year after joining Inter Kashi, he found in Habas a catalyst he had been waiting to process his rebirth with a structure of meaning.If Edmundâs journey to self-realization was marinated in suffering, the one for Habas had a smidge of rejection. Having returned to take charge of Mohun Bagan Super Giant midway in the 2023-2024 season and guided them to the ISL Winnersâ Shield, the veteran Spanish coach didnât find any backers from the team management to continue and took the plunge into the second tier of Indian club football with Inter Kashi.Edmund â already becoming the first player from I-League to earn a call-up in the senior national team since ISLâs promotion to the top league â welcomed the Spaniard to the newly-formed team with a late winner, helping Inter Kashi edge past SC Bengaluru at Kalyani stadium on Nov 24 in 2024. Habas went on to transform his precious pupil from a winger to an attacker, often employing him as a False 9 position. The result was dazzling for the duo and devastating for the rivals. articles.title: Jack Grealish: What does the future hold for the Man City winger?
articles.summary: Man City winger has made two substitute appearances so far this season, but his future remains in doubt.
articles.body:
Jack Grealish is back in the fold at Manchester City ... for now.

The 30-year-old is into the final year of his reported Â£300,000-a-week contract at Etihad Stadium and was discarded by Pep Guardiola in the Spaniard's final season in charge, being allowed to join Everton on a season-long loan deal.

That spell on Merseyside was cut short in January by a foot injury, but the Englishman has returned to full fitness and featured in both of City's games so far this season.

Grealish came on during the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal and played the final eight minutes of City's late comeback win over Bournemouth in Sunday's Premier League opener.

The winger appeared to be in good spirits while sitting on the bench against the Cherries and thanked City fans on social media afterwards for a "nice welcome" on his home return.

Though he has been handed a new lease of life under Guardiola's successor Enzo Maresca, no guarantees are being offered that Grealish will remain a City player come transfer deadline day on Tuesday, 1 September.

'Up front next week?' Maresca's Guehi gamble pays off Published 2 days ago

'Up front next week?' Maresca's Guehi gamble pays off

Options open as Maresca waits 'to see what happens'

Grealish was spotted in training when the City players reported for pre-season in mid-July. He was supposed to join his team-mates on the tour of the Far East but was ruled out after suffering an injury setback.

The former Aston Villa skipper has seen Guardiola's departure as a fresh start and impressed in training to such an extent he has earned a place back in the squad.

Heading into the final week of the transfer window, clubs sources have left all options open for Grealish's future - staying at the club, going out on loan again or leaving permanently.

Maresca has not ruled out a move either, saying after Sunday's game: "He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best.

"Then it is one more week to go and we will see what happens. Not only with Jack but also other players."

Grealish looked to be getting back to his best during his loan at Everton , contributing two goals and six assists in 20 appearances before his injury.

Such was his form at the beginning of last season, he claimed the Premier League's Player of the Month award for August and quickly became a fans' favourite.

City sources say there have been no concrete offers for Grealish so far this summer, with a return to Hill Dickinson Stadium looking the most viable option, should he move away.

Everton are yet to make an approach and try to agree a deal, but he remains of interest to the Toffees.

"He is a player we have remained in contact with," Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear told BBC Radio Merseyside.

"It was no secret he decided to have his injury rehabilitation done here for the remainder of last season - he didn't have to do that as he could have gone back to Manchester City .

"He is a player who has fallen in love with the right shade of blue, but ultimately he is a City player and we have to respect that. What I do know is that the supporters and the team embraced him and treated him as one of our own. That gave us a good platform to have a longer term conversation with him.

"The most important thing is that he is back fit after he had a serious injury, so I was delighted to see him get some minutes in the Community Shield."

articles.title: Aston Villa: Unai Emery's problems mounting ahead of Arsenal test after threadbare squad falls apart against Brighton
articles.summary: Sky Sports analyses the problems mounting for Unai Emery at Aston Villa following their dismal defeat to Brighton in their season opener; Villa lost 4-0 at the Amex Stadium and Joao Gomes was sent off; Emery's side host Arsenal next, live on Monday Night Football
articles.body:
A threadbare Aston Villa squad fell apart against Brighton at the Amex Stadium - and champions Arsenal are on the horizon with problems mounting for Unai Emery.

The Villa boss has been forced to watch on as his Europa League-winning squad has been decimated during the summer transfer window.

Four of the starting line-up from that May final have departed, leaving gaping holes across the pitch, and the situation could worsen before they host Arsenal at Villa Park, live on Monday Night Football.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Aston Villa news & transfers🦁
  • Aston Villa fixtures & scores | FREE Villa highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

The seismic changes caused a storm that even the experienced Emery could not weather on the opening weekend.

Villa became just the second team in Premier League history to concede four goals, receive a red card and score an own goal in the first half - after Southampton against Manchester United in 2020/21. Starts to the season do not get much worse.

Emery has navigated slow starts before: Villa did not score a league goal until September 21 last season only to recover and secure Champions League football, but this feels like his biggest challenge yet.

The situation appears bleak but there is no time for self-pity - changes, adjustments and reinforcements are desperately needed.

From bad to worse? More exits on the horizon

Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa are gone. Ollie Watkins is another big name and cornerstone of the squad approaching an exit amid interest from Al Hilal.

"Ask him. I can only answer it by silence," was the response from Emery when asked why Watkins did not make the trip to the south coast for the defeat at Brighton, as his side unravelled to an embarrassing defeat without a recognised striker named in the squad.

Emiliano Martinez, a stalwart in goal, was also absent and is pursuing an exit after a move to Juventus fell through. His replacement, Zion Suzuki, watched on from the bench as his new side failed to land a blow in the one-sided brawl at the Amex.

Villa's squad retention is the lowest in the Premier League at 65.6 per cent, followed closely by Tottenham at 67.1 per cent.

However, changes at Spurs were needed given back-to-back 17th-placed finishes. Villa's squad has been pulled apart from a point of success.

Joao Gomes, another new recruit and a man Villa were relying on to fill one of the many chasms, was sent off on his league debut at Brighton to add salt to the wound of the dismal defeat.

Record signing Johan Manzambi is yet to make an appearance due to injury and will not be available to face Arsenal, joining Amadou Onana on the sidelines following his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury at the World Cup.

Alejandro Garnacho and Matteo Ruggeri both came off the bench to make their debuts at Brighton, their introductions providing fresh legs more than anything as Emery sought to limit the damage.

Key players have left and their replacements are either unavailable or being kept at arm's length from the upheaval to slowly embed into the team. So, where do Villa turn now?

Toothless - Villa need an option up front

One position that needs addressing sooner rather than later is up front.

Watkins' future at Villa Park is seemingly approaching a bitter and sudden end. The cryptic interview from Emery when quizzed on his absence points to irreparable damage.

Villa turned to Emi Buendia in a false nine role and that experiment, albeit a forced one, panned out as expected as they registered just two touches in the opposition box before the red card and five in total.

They simply cannot approach the game against Arsenal without a focal point of the attack.

Seventeen-year-old Brian Madjo, who emerged in style with five goals in seven appearances throughout pre-season, is out injured and Watkins' usual understudy Tammy Abraham was also sidelined at Brighton.

Sky Sports News has reported the club are expected to act on their long-term interest in reuniting Nicolas Jackson and Emery, his old boss at Villarreal, if Watkins does depart - given the manner of their opening loss and the strength of their next opponent, urgency might be required.

The club have also made an approach to AC Milan for Rafael Leao, with the Portugal forward open to the move.

Villa have spent the least amount of any side in the league to replace the players they have lost this summer - and striker is not a position you can make do without.

Who replaces Joao Gomes in midfield?

Joao Gomes captured the hearts of Villa fans for his performances in pre-season, scoring in the 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich to cap off an impressive start to life in claret and blue.

However, like Villa as a whole, he unravelled against Brighton. Gomes was caught on the ball inside his own penalty area for Jack Hinshelwood's second, scored just 79 seconds after his first and Brighton's third, and the Brazilian was sent off for violent conduct soon after.

He will now serve a three-game suspension, giving Emery another headache.

His arrival was meant to ease the absence of Tielemans' departure but Emery will now have to rely on Ross Barkley, John McGinn, Lamare Bogarde or potentially Lindelof in midfield, as he did in the Europa League final.

Gomes was embraced by his manager as he trudged off the pitch after 40-minute Premier League debut to forget. A difficult afternoon for all involved but the problems have only worsened as a result of his red card.

A deal is currently being finalised to sign free agent Leon Goretzka and his experience, as well as leadership, is needed. Whether he could be thrust into the line-up against Arsenal remains to be seen.

Worrying insight into life without Konsa

The absence of a recognised striker at Brighton meant Villa's struggles going forward were to be expected. The defensive performance, on the other hand, was inexcusable.

Konsa's £55m move to Arsenal was arguably the most worrying of all the summer exits. The defending at the Amex offered a worrying insight into what life without the centre-back could be like.

Self-inflicted errors from Pau Torres, Lindelof failing to track runners in the box, and the lack of calmness that Villa would often rely on when Konsa was a pillar of the defence all contributed to the embarrassing display inside their own penalty box.

Brighton cut through their opponents with ease, so much so that they registered the highest expected goals tally from open play that Emery has faced since being appointed to the role in October 2022 (3.54 xG).

A bid has been rejected for Southampton centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis and contact has been made for Club Brugge defender Joel Ordanez but in the meantime, before the cavalry arrives, Villa have to cut out the individual errors.

Three of the 21 shots Brighton had came from Villa errors, of which two resulted in goals. If the same pattern unfolds at Villa Park, Arsenal will waste no time in replicating a similar onslaught.

The problems for Villa have piled up and while certain solutions are seemingly being worked on in the background, Emery and his threadbare squad may be forced to prove they can manage without them against the champions.

articles.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools
articles.summary: Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences
articles.body:
Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.

York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.

"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.

They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.

When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.

A San Francisco 49ers statement read: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.

Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.

articles.summary: Chelsea are morphing into a new team under Sonia Bompastor; they are taking learning from a disappointing 2025/26 season, with a clear change in playing personnel; they want to return to WSL and domestic glory, as well as competing in the Champions League
articles.body:
"Chelsea are going through a transitional moment and it takes time for the club to rebuild."

Not pundit analysis, but the thoughts of Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor to Sky Sports ahead of the new WSL season.

And despite the hint of cliché, it works. There has been plenty upheaval over the last two years, starting with Bompastor replacing Emma Hayes.

Then, there was the shock departure of Paul Green as head of women's football in February. Alongside Hayes, the duo oversaw years of unprecedented success. It is something hard to sustain and even harder to replicate.

But that is the task that falls at Bompastor's feet. She managed to keep it going in her first season with an unbeaten domestic treble - some may say with Hayes' influence still in play - but her second campaign exposed the realties. Chelsea were not the team of old and a new era was beckoning.

Now in her third pre-season with the Blues, Bompastor believes she has the backing of the club to do just that.

"I think now I understand what the club is about a lot more," she said. "I also understand what we want to achieve and bringing my input into that.

"It's good to be in a place where I feel the confidence and the trust coming from the hierarchy in the club. As much as I know my job, we need to get good results in order for me to stay as long as possible, but it's also important to feel like we also have time to rebuild the team in order for us to compete against the best."

How last season informs the next

Chelsea only won the League Cup last season and finished third in the league behind Manchester City and Arsenal. It was the first time in six years they had not walked away with the WSL title.

Bompastor reflected: "We wanted last season to be a more successful season because Chelsea is a club who is used to winning. We only won one trophy, but if you analyse it, we have some good learnings to take and that's really important for us to reflect on.

"We spoke a lot about the environment and the culture we want to create here at Chelsea.

"It's a lot about standards, behaviours, how you show up every day, how much you are committing to work hard to achieve your goals and what are the type of behaviours you want to show up every day, off and on pitch.

"Who do we want to be as a team? How do we want people to talk about Chelsea? These things are really important for us to be able to achieve the goals we have.

"Chelsea are a club who are used to winning and we need to make sure we put everything together in order for us to achieve that.

"I'm quite happy with the squad of players I have, the quality we have, but it's also important alongside that quality to bring the right mentality."

Experience and youth informing transfer policy

This summer does have the air of a new start about it, especially in terms of playing personnel.

Players who have been the face of Chelsea for years have left. Former captain Millie Bright retired, legendary goalscorer Sam Kerr moved to the USA. Niamh Charles, Guro Reiten and Johanna Rytting Kaneryd also departed. They represent years of service, experience and trophies.

"We lost some really important players in terms of the environment and culture," Bompastor said. "Some of them had been here for many years and it's difficult to replace them.

"So it's for us, the staff and club, to think about how and what is the best way to replace them. It's about the recruitment, but also again linked back to the environment and the culture we want to create.

"We have also great leaders who have the right mentality about when you are on pitch, it's about winning games. Off the pitch, it's about the behaviours you need and showing up every day in order for us to work hard on the pitch to achieve the goals."

Chelsea's transfer strategy of mixing experience and youth is clear and epitomised by two of their four summer signings so far in Katie McCabe and Nelly Las.

McCabe needs little introduction. Indeed, Bompastor herself told Sky Sports she did not need to speak on the defender's quality, and it is clear she goes a long way in replacing some of the leadership Chelsea lost.

"She has already started to impact the squad in terms of the behaviours and the standards," Bompastor added. "I'm really pleased she's a Chelsea player now."

Las, meanwhile, is an exciting 18-year-old prospect who joined from Leicester. She made 16 WSL appearances across the last two seasons, and has featured for England's youth teams.

"It's important to have the right balance between experienced players, but also the youth into the squad," Bompastor said. "Players having versatility to play in different positions is also really important for me.

"I'm a manager who really loves to work with young players, to invest time to develop them and I'm really keen to bring these players into the squad and see how they can develop to contribute to the success we will have in the future."

Carrying on a legacy

There will always be pressure to win at Chelsea given their history, and they now have a balance to strike - maintaining that legacy while also forging a new way forward and meeting the standards Bompastor has set out.

That falls, in part, to the team's senior players - no matter how long they have played for the club.

One of those is defender Ellie Carpenter. She may have only been at Chelsea for a year, but as a multiple-trophy winner and regular starter, she will likely now step into a leadership role among the group.

"Chelsea are going through a bit of a transition phase at the moment. A lot of legends have gone and they left such a great legacy," she told Sky Sports. "Now it's our turn to do that, follow in their footsteps and to build on what Chelsea is as a club.

"As a footballer, you love those opportunities and moments in your career and it's a perfect time to be stepping into that role for this club.

"Our aim this season is to fight for those trophies back and show what Chelsea is about. We want to do it as a team, winning in that way and enjoying it and hopefully getting the results on the way as well.

"We have a great team this season and pre-season has felt good so I'm excited."

Champions League - is this the year?

One way this squad can cement themselves into Chelsea history is by winning the one trophy that continues to elude them - the Champions League.

For a long time, the Blues' recruitment strategy has been geared towards European glory while the domestic trophies took care of themselves.

Bompastor won it as a manager with Lyon and was a key reason for her appointment in 2024. Carpenter was in her victorious squad, as was new striker Melvine Malard and defender Kadeisha Buchanan. McCabe won it with Arsenal. Lucy Bronze - who signed a new Chelsea deal this summer - has been crowned Europe champion five times.

But none of those have come in Chelsea blue and every year, we ask the same question: is this the year the wait is over?

"Winning the Champions League is one of the main goals for us," Bompastor said. "We'll work as hard as possible to achieve that and I know everyone is expecting Chelsea to always be at their best.

"But the competition now in Europe is getting higher and higher. Many clubs now are in a position where they can compete to win the Champions League. I don't want to shy away from us and our ambitions, but I also know it's difficult.

"But that's the one trophy we're missing in the club and we will try as hard as possible to fight for that."

"It's always what Chelsea want," Carpenter added. "It's what their ambition is, what the fans want, what everyone here wants and what we work towards every day.

"This squad is young, but multiple people have won it in the team, so that helps a lot to bring the experience and what it takes to win.

"But we're just going to go game-by-game this season. We don't want to put too much pressure on ourselves. When we're enjoying football, we're playing our best football."

Getting comfortable with scrutiny

While it may seem a tedious back and forth on the Champions League each year, that is the kind of scrutiny that comes with being at Chelsea and despite changes elsewhere, will never alter.

It has perhaps been one of the learnings for Bompastor in her two years at the club, and something she must instil in the squad she is assembling.

"I've never been in a place before where the scrutiny is so high like at Chelsea, but I'm comfortable with it," she reflected.

"It means people care about us and really think we are a really important club. That's what comes with our standards and Chelsea being one of the best clubs in the world, so we need to get comfortable with that.

"We need to make sure when we go into the season, we don't have any regrets and we give our all any time we step into the pitch."

What is for sure is the Blues are in the process of morphing into something new. Consistent evolution was one of the secrets to Hayes' success, and Bompastor will be hoping the same is true now.

articles.title: Premier League 2026/27, Gameweek 1: Record-breaking numbers that headlined sensational season opener
articles.summary: Football News: Explore the dramatic opening weekend of the Premier League 2026/27 season, featuring record-setting goals, historic victories, and key player milestones.
articles.body: The 2026/27 Premier League season is officially underway, with Gameweek 1 already producing landmark results, dramatic late goals and a host of eye-catching individual milestones. From Hull Cityâs historic win over Manchester United to Liverpoolâs long unbeaten run on the opening matchday and Arsenalâs dominant start, here are some of the key numbers and storylines from the opening weekend.150 | ARTETA REACHES ANOTHER LANDMARKArsenal began their title defence with a convincing 3-0 win over newly promoted Coventry City, while Mikel Arteta reached 150 Premier League victories as Arsenal manager.Arteta reached the landmark in 249 games, putting him among an elite group of managers to reach 150 Premier League wins in fewer than 250 matches.The result also extended Arsenal's remarkable record against promoted opposition. The Gunners are now unbeaten in 46 consecutive Premier League home games against promoted sides, with 41 wins and five draws. They have won their last 17 such matches, scoring 47 goals and conceding just nine.Martin Ãdegaard also made an early mark, scoring in consecutive appearances for Arsenal for the first time since December 2023. His two goals already this season have surpassed his total of one goal in 36 appearances across all competitions last season.71.6% | MANCHESTER UNITED HAVE THE BALL, BUT HULL HAVE THE HISTORYOne of the biggest shocks of the opening weekend came at Hull City, where the newly promoted side defeated Manchester United 2-0.United had 71.6% possession, their highest in a Premier League match since September 2023, but could not find the net.The defeat was historic. It was the first time in Manchester United's league history that they had lost their opening fixture to a newly promoted side. United have now lost their opening Premier League match in four of the last seven seasons.Their attacking frustration was highlighted by another number: United have failed to score on the opening day in back-to-back Premier League seasons, despite registering a combined 43 shots across those matches.For Hull, meanwhile, the win ended a long wait against United. They had gone without scoring in their previous 37 attempts against the Red Devils in the competition before Semi Ajayi found the net. Hull's victory was also their first league win over United since 1974.14 | LIVERPOOL'S OPENING-DAY STREAK SURVIVES ANOTHER THRILLERLiverpool's new era under Andoni Iraola began with a dramatic 2-2 draw at Newcastle, but one remarkable streak remained intact.Liverpool are now unbeaten on the opening day of the Premier League season for 14 consecutive campaigns, the longest active run in the competition.Newcastle's wait for a victory over Liverpool, however, continues. They are now without a win in their last 20 Premier League meetings with Liverpool, recording six draws and 14 defeats since their last victory in December 2015The fixture has also developed a remarkable late-goal pattern. This was the fourth consecutive Premier League meeting between the sides at St James' Park to feature a result-changing goal in the 90th minute or later.Dominik Szoboszlai's stoppage-time penalty came at 98:06, making it Liverpool's latest-ever Premier League penalty, while giving the visitors a dramatic point.40 | ELANGA AND WILLOCK FINALLY END LONG GOAL DROUGHTSGameweek 1 was also a weekend for players ending lengthy waits for goals.Anthony Elanga scored his first Premier League goal for Newcastle on his 33rd top-flight appearance for the club, ending a run of 40 Premier League appearances without a goal.Joe Willock also found the net against Liverpool, scoring his first Premier League goal since February 2024. His goal ended a drought of 61 appearances and 40 shots without scoring in the competition.Newcastle's late collapse against Liverpool also continued another unwanted trend. They have dropped 29 points from winning positions in the Premier League since the start of last season, the second-most among teams in Europe's big-five leagues during that period, behind Wolfsburg's 33.1993/94 | IPSWICH END LONG WAITIpswich Town marked their return to the Premier League with a dramatic 2-1 win over Sunderland, secured by Jack Clarke's 90th-minute winner.The victory was Ipswich's first opening-day Premier League win since 1993/94, ending a wait of more than three decades.It also ended a run of nine consecutive top-flight defeats at Portman Road.There was another debut milestone in the match, with Emersonn becoming the first player to score on his overall Premier League debut for Ipswich since Fabian Wilnis in August 2000.26 | TOTTENHAM HAVE THE BALL, BUT BRENTFORD HAVE THE SHOTSTottenham endured one of the weekendâs heaviest defeats, going down 3-0 to Brentford. Spurs had 59.8% possession but still conceded 26 shots, highlighting the disconnect between having the ball and controlling the game. It was the highest possession recorded by a team to face more than 25 shots in a Premier League match since records began in 2003/04.The result matched Spursâ joint-heaviest defeat on the opening day of a Premier League season, equalling their 3-0 loss to Manchester United in 2011/12. For Brentford, meanwhile, it was their biggest-ever win in the top flight, with their attacking dominance reflected in an xG of 3.96, their highest in a Premier League match since January 2025.4 | EVERTON END FOUR YEARS OF OPENING-DAY FRUSTRATIONEverton also began the campaign with a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, ending their opening-day drought.The result was Everton's first opening-day Premier League victory since August 2021, following four consecutive defeats without scoring.Iliman Ndiaye continued his growing importance to the side. Since joining Everton in 2024/25, he has been involved in 19 Premier League goals, scoring 15 and providing four assists, the most goal involvements of any Everton player during that period.Despite losing, Crystal Palace created plenty of opportunities, recording an xG of 2.04, their highest in a Premier League game without scoring since December 2018. 5 | STACHâS LONG-RANGE THREAT LEADS THE WAYLeeds United began their campaign with a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest, extending another impressive opening-day run.Leeds have now won their opening Premier League fixture in three consecutive campaigns, matching their longest such run in the competition.They have also won five of their last eight Premier League games, collecting 17 points during that run. Only Arsenal, with 18 points, have collected more points since the start of April.Anton Stach was again a threat from distance. He has scored five Premier League goals from outside the penalty area since the start of last season, more than any other player.He also has four direct free-kick goals during that period, joint-most among all players.2 | PROMOTED SIDES MAKE STRONG RETURNTwo of the three promoted clubs won their opening fixtures, a feat that had previously occurred only four times in Premier League history.That gives the opening weekend an interesting early storyline: the promoted sides have arrived in the Premier League with little interest in simply making up the numbers.31 | CHELSEA START THE SEASON AT A SPRINTChelsea closed out the opening weekend with a 3-1 victory over Fulham, and they did not waste any time getting started. JoÃ£o Pedro's opener after just 31 seconds was the earliest-ever goal scored by a team in its opening game of a Premier League season.It was also Chelsea's fastest Premier League goal since Pedro scored after 30 seconds against Manchester United in October 2016. Chelsea have now scored 13 goals in the opening minute of Premier League matches, with only Everton having more, at 14.The result also gave Xabi Alonso a winning start to his Premier League career at Chelsea. He became the first Blues manager since Maurizio Sarri in 2018 to see Chelsea score three goals in his first Premier League game in charge.For Chelsea, the victory ended a wait for an opening-day win. The Blues had not won their first Premier League game of the season since 2022/23, when they defeated Everton 1-0.Chelsea's starting XI had an average age of just 24 years and 43 days, making it the youngest starting XI fielded by any team on the opening weekend.The Gameweek 1 numbers at a glance:150 | Arteta's Premier League wins46 | Arsenal's unbeaten home games vs promoted sides71.6% | Man Utd possession vs Hull4 | United's opening-day defeats in the last seven seasons14 | Liverpool's consecutive unbeaten opening days20 | Newcastle games without beating Liverpool98:06 | Szoboszlai's late penalty40 | Elanga's appearances without a goal61 | Willock's appearances without a goal1993/94 | Ipswich's previous opening-day win3.96 | Brentford's xG vs Tottenham31 seconds | JoÃ£o Pedro's record opening goal13 | Chelsea's opening-minute goals24 years, 43 days | Chelsea's youngest starting XI of GW1124 | Chelsea's consecutive games without a player aged 30+ featuringGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Carlos Baleba transfer: Manchester United complete signing of Cameroon midfielder from Brighton
articles.summary: Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they enquired about signing him during the January transfer window; the Cameroon international signs a five-year deal at Old Trafford
articles.body:
Manchester United have completed the signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton.

The Cameroon international, 22, joins the club in a deal worth up to £70m, made up of a £65m guaranteed fee plus £5m in add-ons.

He has signed a five-year contract which includes the option of a further year.

Baleba is currently injured, having picked up an ankle injury in pre-season, but Sky Sports News understands he could be back by mid-September. Manchester United play Manchester City on September 13, live on Sky Sports.

  • Man Utd fixtures & scores | FREE Man Utd highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Baleba's arrival at Old Trafford brings an end to a transfer saga that has lasted almost 12 months. Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they enquired about signing him during the January transfer window.

He remained one of United's top targets this summer and becomes their third addition in midfield after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

"It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour," Baleba told the club's website.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

Baleba joined Brighton from Lille in 2023 and made 112 appearances for the club. He featured 35 times last season and was absent for a spell while representing Cameroon at the Africa Cup of Nations.

'I had no idea what this club would become' - Baleba pens Brighton farewell

Upon the announcement of the news, Baleba took to social media to post an emotional farewell to Brighton.

"I came here at 19 with little English and no idea what this club would become to me," he wrote.

"Brighton only asked me to be myself. The staff who make the club run so well. The team-mates who took the time to understand me, on the pitch and off it. The nights at the Amex when I heard my name from that stand always made me feel at home.

"To all of the fans, staff and my team-mates. You looked after me and for that I will hold you all close to my heart. Wherever I play, this club is in how I play. Good luck Seagulls."

Is Baleba a major gamble or a game-changer for Man Utd?

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

A year ago, Carlos Baleba appeared to have the world at his feet.

A breakout season at Brighton had established the then-21-year-old as one of the Premier League's most coveted young midfielders, with a move to one of Europe's elite clubs seemingly inevitable. Manchester United were among those interested, having identified Baleba as a potential transformative presence in midfield.

But Brighton's reported £100m-plus valuation proved a stumbling block. The move never materialised and Baleba stayed at the Amex.

His form subsequently dipped dramatically. His numbers fell and, at times, he looked a shadow of the midfielder who had generated so much excitement the previous season.

That makes this a gamble for United. But, stylistically, there are few midfielders better suited to what they need.

United require greater authority in the middle of the pitch and, crucially, someone capable of winning the ball back in deeper areas. Baleba brings exactly that. His athleticism, aggression and ability to carry the ball through midfield would add a level of dynamism and steel that is currently missing.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been astute additions, but Baleba offers something different: specialist defensive power coupled with the athleticism to drive United up the pitch.

His age is another major factor. Baleba is still only 22 and, despite his inconsistent season, there remains a belief around him that he can develop into one of the world's best midfielders.

That ambition is reflected in his influences. Baleba has spoken of his admiration for Paul Pogba, Yaya Toure and Andres Iniesta, while Neymar and Ronaldinho were among his favourite players to watch. There is a desire for self-expression in his game that goes beyond the physical qualities that made so highly rated.

There is risk attached to signing him. United would be betting on the player Baleba can become rather than simply the one he has been over the past 12 months.

But if United want to find a midfielder capable of growing into one of the best in his position, this is exactly the sort of gamble they should be willing to take.

articles.title: Tennessee LB Arion Carter's Suspension Over $427 Flight Reduced by NCAA
articles.summary: Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter had his suspension regarding a flight payment reduced to one game by the NCAA, Volunteers athletic director Danny White announced Tuesday.
articles.body:
Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter had his suspension regarding a flight payment reduced to one game by the NCAA, Volunteers athletic director Danny White announced Tuesday.

Carter initially received a two-game suspension on July 29 after his agent paid $427 for a flight to an NFL training facility during the offseason. He later paid the agent back for the flight.

The NCAA originally suspended Carter three games for the Level III violation before the Volunteers appealed the penalty and had it reduced, according to ESPN's Mark Schlabach .

The 21-year-old played through a foot injury near the end of last season and declared for the 2026 NFL draft in Dec. 2025, but ultimately returned to Tennessee after aggravating the injury and undergoing surgery.

Carter is expected to be a key piece of a deep Volunteers linebacking corps that includes Amare Campbell, Edwin Spillman and Jeremiah Telander.

In 10 games last season, Carter racked up 76 tackles, six tackles for loss, two passes defended, 1.5 sacks and one forced fumble.

Tennessee is looking to remain a threat in the SEC during its 2026 campaign after recording double-digit win totals in two of the past four years.

While Carter will still miss the Volunteers' season-opening clash with Furman on Sept. 5, he'll now be available to suit up during a matchup with Georgia Tech on Sept. 12.

articles.title: Liam Delap: Nottingham Forest agree Â£50m deal for Chelsea striker
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest have agreed a fee worth around Â£50m to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap.
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record fee worth around Â£50m to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

The 23-year-old is expected to undergo a medical and sign a long-term contract at the City Ground this week.

Delap's move comes a year after he joined Chelsea from Ipswich Town for Â£30m amid competition from Manchester United and Everton .

However, Chelsea made him available for sale this summer after he scored just one Premier League goal in a previous campaign disrupted by shoulder and hamstring injuries.

Forest have already signed defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting for Â£34m, alongside free agents, Austrian midfielder Xaver Schlager and goalkeeper Steve Benda.

They sold England midfielder Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for a club-record Â£116m and striker Taiwo Awoniyi to Coventry City for Â£9m.

Delap's arrival would provide competition for strikers Chris Wood and Igor Jesus, who failed to find the target in Forest's 1-0 defeat by Leeds in their home Premier League opener on Saturday.

Chelsea have also signed two strikers this summer in Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg and Danny Welbeck from Brighton .

Delap came up through Derby County's youth system before joining Manchester City in 2019.

After helping City win the FA Youth Cup in the 2019-20 campaign, he scored 24 goals in 20 Premier League 2 matches in 2020-21 as they won the title.

In September 2020 the striker scored on his senior City debut in a 2-1 League Cup win against Bournemouth , and three days later made his Premier League debut in a 5-2 defeat by Leicester.

Injuries played a part in limiting further first-team opportunities, and between 2022 and 2024 Delap spent time on loan in the Championship with Stoke, Preston North End and Hull City .

In the summer of 2024 he was sold for Â£20m by City to Ipswich and scored 12 goals in 37 Premier League games for the newly promoted side.

articles.title: Bradley Barcola transfer news: Liverpool hold fresh talks with PSG over France international ahead of transfer deadline
articles.summary: Liverpool hold positive talks with PSG over Bradley Barcola; there is optimism that a deal can be struck for the winger; there has been a gap in valuation between two clubs throughout summer, with PSG asking for around £145m for Barcola; Reds also interested in PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye
articles.body:
Liverpool are holding further talks with Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday for Bradley Barcola.

There has been a gap in valuation between the two clubs throughout the summer, with PSG asking for around £145m for the France international.

However, the discussions that have taken place during this window have been described as positive, and there is optimism that a deal can be struck with a week left before the deadline.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Liverpool news & transfers🔴
  • Liverpool fixtures & scores | FREE Liverpool highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Sky Sports News understands there are good relations between the two clubs at the highest level. It is hoped this will help Liverpool and PSG reach an agreement.

Liverpool have also explored a move for Barcola's team-mate, Ibrahim Mbaye, who plays off the right wing.

The Premier League club's priority throughout this window has been to reinforce in wide areas.

They have been pursuing Barcola and Mbaye, while Brighton have also rejected two Liverpool offers for Yankuba Minteh, the latest being £60m.

Liverpool are currently the only club chasing Barcola, who has entered the final two years of his deal and has grown dissatisfied with his role at the European champions.

Liverpool, meanwhile, do not want to sell Cody Gakpo amid interest from Tottenham and Manchester City and would likely need two new wingers in before considering letting the Netherlands international go.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin Reacts to 'Villain' Label After Recruiting NFL's Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris to LSU
articles.summary: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin isn't concerned with labels as he tries to restore his team to national championship contention.
articles.body:
LSU head coach Lane Kiffin isn't concerned with labels as he tries to restore his team to national championship contention.

During an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday, Kiffin was asked about the "villain" label he's received since landing commitments from former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright and former New Orleans Saints defensive end Zxavian Harrison."

"I don't worry too much about that," Kiffin replied. "I think as you talk about villains, sometimes the difference between the hero and the villain isn't very far apart, and it changes very often. ... When you're trying to do things at the highest level, a lot of times people want you to apologize for what you're doing when you're chasing greatness."

According to the Associated Press , Wright was among a group of athletes who filed a lawsuit in Louisiana seeking a fifth year of college eligibility for members of the high school class of 2022. The court issued a temporary restraining order that paved the way for him and others to return to college athletics.

Kiffin noted on Tuesday that he's not the only coach who is trying to make use of the loopholes in the NCAA's eligibility rules.

Kiffin went on to add that while he understands the concerns about professional athletes trying to gain advantages by returning to college, he feels that doesn't apply to this situation because of the specific circumstances surrounding the 2022 class' chances of a fifth year of eligibility.

"There's a lot of parts that I don't like within that. I don't think professionals should come back to college sports and college football, particularly," Kiffin said. "But in this instance, this is not professionals that have gone and played seasons or just randomly filed an injunction in a state to become eligible. This is part of a specific class that was ruled wronged by the NCAA that was supposed to be five for five."

Still, the situation undoubtedly creates more questions than answers in the ever-changing landscape of college sports, so it will be interesting to see how the NCAA responds going forward.

articles.title: Julian Alvarez transfer latest: Atletico standing firm on Barcelona as Arsenal become only get out for Argentine striker
articles.summary: Julian Alvarez is holding out for a move to Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid are standing firm on the refusal to sell to their LaLiga rivals; Atletico football expert Ruben Uría believes the only way out for Alvarez is to join Premier League champions Arsenal
articles.body:
Julian Alvarez must take one of two paths before the transfer deadline: stay at Atletico Madrid and try to rebuild his connection with the fans or get his head around a potential move to Arsenal.

Atletico have told him again that they will not sell him to Barcelona and that - coupled with the reaction of the club's supporters on Sunday - has left him "devastated", according to well-placed sources in Spain.

The situation is now "extremely tense", according to Atletico expert and journalist Ruben Uría.

"Neither Miguel Gil Marín (CEO of Atlético Madrid) nor the Apollo board want to sell the player to Barcelona," he told Sky Sports News. "The entire Apollo board supports Gil Marín's decision. Alvarez has been told."

According to Uría, Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has remained in contact with his former Atletico employers in recent days after Alvarez was booed off by supporters in the opening LaLiga game against Villarreal.

But Arsenal will need Alvarez to put Barcelona out of his mind and show he really wants to join Mikel Arteta's project before any serious negotiations or any offers can be made. In that vein, Arsenal are not currently hopeful of getting him in before September 1 and they are certainly not currently expecting it at the Emirates.

  • Arsenal fixtures & scores | FREE Arsenal highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱

Alvarez still has his heart set on Barcelona. The question is, will this be the case as the transfer window comes to an end? Will the deadline have any effect? Arsenal will always be ready and open to Alvarez should he change his mind but, at the moment, any move looks very unlikely.

Julian Alvarez must take one of two paths before the transfer deadline: stay at Atletico Madrid and try to rebuild his connection with the fans or get his head around a potential move to Arsenal.

Atletico have told him again that they will not sell him to Barcelona and that - coupled with the reaction of the club's supporters on Sunday - has left him "devastated", according to well-placed sources in Spain.

The situation is now "extremely tense", according to Atletico expert and journalist Ruben Uría.

"Neither Miguel Gil Marín (CEO of Atlético Madrid) nor the Apollo board want to sell the player to Barcelona," he told Sky Sports News. "The entire Apollo board supports Gil Marín's decision. Alvarez has been told."

According to Uría, Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has remained in contact with his former Atletico employers in recent days after Alvarez was booed off by supporters in the opening LaLiga game against Villarreal.

But Arsenal will need Alvarez to put Barcelona out of his mind and show he really wants to join Mikel Arteta's project before any serious negotiations or any offers can be made. In that vein, Arsenal are not currently hopeful of getting him in before September 1 and they are certainly not currently expecting it at the Emirates.

articles.title: Former Man Utd star and pundit warns Neymar-Messi reunion will turn MLS into âeven more of a circusâ in scathing attack
articles.summary: Football News: Giuseppe Rossi warns that Neymar's potential transfer to Inter Miami for a reunion with Messi and Suarez could make MLS 'even more of a circus' while failing to address the league's competitive issues.
articles.body: Neymar's potential move to Inter Miami has been framed as the perfect opportunity for another reunion with Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez, but one former Premier League and Serie A forward believes the move could expose a bigger problem within Major League Soccer.Giuseppe Rossi, the former Manchester United and Villarreal forward who is now Head of Soccer at the New York Cosmos, has warned that bringing Neymar to MLS would be excellent entertainment and marketing, but would do little to improve the quality of football being played in the competition.The Brazilian has been repeatedly linked with a move to Miami, where he could reunite with Messi and Suarez after their hugely successful spell together at Barcelona. For Rossi, however, the question is not whether supporters would want to watch it. It is whether another superstar reunion is actually helping MLS become a stronger football league.Rossi questions what MLS is trying to becomeRossi made his comments while speaking to GOAL in an interview conducted in association with BetBrothers, and he was particularly critical of the league's continued reliance on globally famous players to generate attention.MLS has undergone a major transformation through marquee arrivals over the years, with David Beckham, Steven Gerrard, Kaka, Andrea Pirlo, Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Wayne Rooney among the established stars who have moved to the United States.Messi's arrival in 2023 took that strategy to another level, with the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner becoming the league's biggest attraction. Inter Miami subsequently surrounded him with several former Barcelona team-mates, including Suarez, Sergio Busquets and Jordi Alba, while Rodrigo De Paul and Casemiro have also joined the club.Neymar could now become the latest superstar to make the move, with his Santos contract due to expire at the end of the year.But Rossi believes MLS risks becoming too focused on the attention generated by those names.âThis is where MLS are making mistakes, and they continue to make these mistakes. Itâs great marketing, it is what it is, but what kind of product are you putting on the field?â Rossi told GOAL.He specifically questioned the idea of bringing Neymar to Miami simply to recreate the famous Barcelona attack.âBringing Neymar back to reunite him with Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez, what are you trying to become as a league?ââYouâre moving at a snailâs paceâRossi's concern is not that MLS has failed commercially. Quite the opposite.He acknowledged the league's substantial growth and the increasing value of its clubs, but argued that the sporting product has not developed at the same rate.âIf itâs to get to the level of the big boys out in Europe like the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga and those competitions, youâre moving at a snailâs pace but MLS is very thirsty for clicks and views, and they donât really care about the standard of the football itself,â he said.Rossi went on to distinguish between the league's commercial success and its footballing development.âYes, they have made great strides, and well done to them for that. The valuations of the clubs are high and itâs a great business model but what about the football? Is that growing and moving forward? I donât think so, and thatâs something that has to change.âHe believes the underlying issue comes from the priorities of those running the competition.âThe problem is that the people in charge donât really care. They only care about the valuations. Thatâs the problem when you put these billionaires in charge of a league.âIn Rossi's view, Neymar would therefore be an attractive commercial addition without necessarily addressing the competitive development he believes MLS needs.âTheyâd love to see Neymar come to MLS and play with Messi again but itâs not going to grow MLS as a football league. Thatâs what I think.âRossi still believes Neymar could benefit from joining Messi and SuarezDespite his criticism, Rossi was not arguing that Neymar is finished as a footballer.Quite the opposite: he believes the Brazilian could still make a significant impact if he moved to Inter Miami and reunited with Messi and Suarez.Neymar, now 34, has endured a difficult period with injuries and inconsistent form since leaving European football, and his return to Santos has not produced the sustained revival many expected.But Rossi remains convinced that the player retains the ability to make the move worthwhile on an individual level.âIf Neymar could make the move to Miami, why not? It would be great for him, and heâs still a great player. I freaking love Neymar,â Rossi told GOAL.He added that Neymar remains âone of the best players of his generationâ and that supporters would naturally want to see him back alongside Messi and Suarez.That is precisely where Rossi sees the contradiction: the reunion could be fantastic for the players, the supporters and the headlines, while simultaneously doing little to address what he sees as MLS's sporting shortcomings.âI just look at it another way because there are pros and cons to everything, and yes everybody wants to see Neymar but it does take away from the integrity of the products itself by making MLS into even more of a circus than a true football league.âThe prospect of another MSN reunionNeymar, Messi and Suarez previously formed one of the most devastating attacking partnerships in modern football at Barcelona.Between 2013 and 2017, Neymar scored 105 goals and provided 76 assists in 186 appearances across all competitions for Barcelona, helping the club win eight trophies, including the 2014-15 treble.The possibility of seeing the three together again, this time in MLS, would therefore carry enormous global appeal.For Inter Miami, it would represent another blockbuster addition to a squad that has increasingly become a collection of some of the defining players of the modern era.For MLS, though, Rossi believes the question should go beyond whether another superstar can generate clicks, ticket sales and commercial interest.His warning is essentially about what happens after the spectacle: if the league wants to close the gap with Europe's strongest competitions, he believes improving the football itself has to matter just as much as attracting the biggest names.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: âErling Haaland leaving Man City one day is inevitableâ: Ex-Man City star predicts when striker could push for exit
articles.summary: Football News: Former Man City star Gareth Barry predicts Erling Haaland's eventual departure from the club, discussing the impact of the team's performance on the striker's future. Find out why the next two years are crucial for Haaland and Man City.
articles.body: Erling Haaland's future at Manchester City may be secure for now, but one former City midfielder believes the Norwegian's long-term stay at the Etihad should not be taken for granted.Haaland has committed himself to the club on a contract running until 2034 and remains the centrepiece of City's attack. Yet with the club entering a new era and facing questions over whether it can maintain the dominance of recent seasons, Gareth Barry believes the next couple of years could be decisive in determining whether the prolific striker eventually looks for a new challengeWhy Haaland could eventually look elsewhereHaaland joined City in 2022 and has already established himself as one of the most prolific goalscorers in the club's history.The 26-year-old has scored 162 goals in 200 appearances across all competitions for City, while playing a major role in a period that included a historic Treble in 2022-23. His long-term contract, signed in 2024, was designed to keep one of football's most coveted strikers at the Etihad well into the next decade.But Barry does not believe the length of that agreement necessarily means Haaland will see it through.Speaking exclusively to GOAL, the former England international said: âErling Haaland leaving Man City one day is inevitable.âBarry stressed that Haaland has no reason to force an exit while City remain competitive, and expects the striker to avoid the kind of public agitation that has accompanied some high-profile transfers.âAs much as Haaland's association with City is really big, and that will keep him there for now, he won't be rocking the boat like you see a lot of other players doing,â Barry said.The former City player believes the situation could change if the club's trophy haul begins to decline.âI think if City's dominance does wane a little bit and the trophies aren't coming in, it will fuel the speculation,â he explained. âIt is natural sometimes to want a new challenge, and I'm sure Haaland will be no different.âBarry's prediction is therefore less about Haaland wanting out immediately and more about what happens around him.âIt's not just going to happen overnight. Haaland will think about his career, which is short,â he said. âBut if the trophies aren't coming in, it will just fuel speculation.âAnd given Haaland's standing in the game, Barry expects the striker to have no shortage of options if he eventually decides the time is right.âHe will have offers from all over the world because he's the best striker in the world, so it's just natural. It's one you can see happening in the future.âThe next two years could be crucialFor Barry, the most important period may not be the end of Haaland's current contract but the next two seasons.He believes the striker's eventual decision will be heavily influenced by how competitive City remain domestically and in Europe.âA lot will depend on how competitive City are in Europe and the Premier League in the next year or two, I should imagine,â Barry said.That is particularly significant given the changes taking place around Haaland.Pep Guardiola has departed after his long spell in charge, while City are now entering a new era under Enzo Maresca. At the same time, Rodri has left, removing one of the most influential players from the team's midfield.Those developments have led Barry to question whether City can immediately return to the top of the Premier League.Barry expects Arsenal to be favouritesCity have gone two seasons without winning the Premier League, with Liverpool and then Arsenal restoring themselves to the top of the domestic game.Barry, who helped City win their first Premier League title in 2011-12, believes the latest changes could make a title challenge even more difficult.âEven before selling Rodri, given the turnover of managers at City, it would have been tough to overturn Arsenal from where they are at the moment,â he told GOAL.âI think with Rodri going, they're even less of a threat now to challenge Arsenal.âBarry expects City to strengthen further and believes new additions could ease the burden on Elliot Anderson and the rest of the midfield, but he does not think that will necessarily be enough to make them favourites.âI'm sure they're going to sign one or two to improve and maybe replace him, which will help [Elliot] Anderson and the other players in that midfield,â he said. âI'd say they have less of a chance to challenge and maybe win the title now Rodri is gone. I won't say they've given the title away, but itâs making it a lot harder.âHis assessment of the title race is emphatic.âI have Arsenal down as huge favourites,â Barry said. âI just feel with City, with what's going on, the threat is less and less this season and Rodri leaving has just added to that, really. So I can see the other clubs improving.âHe also expects Chelsea to progress after missing out on Champions League football, while believing Manchester United and Aston Villa could find European competition challenging.Ultimately, Barry still expects City to finish second but sees a sizeable gap between them and Arsenal.âI still think City will possibly be in second place, but they'll be less of a threat than they were last year,â he said.Spain remains a possible destinationHaaland's future has already been linked with the two biggest clubs in Spain.Real Madrid's long-standing pursuit of elite attacking talent means the Norwegian continues to be associated with a potential move to the Santiago BernabÃ©u, while Barcelona are also expected to consider options for the No. 9 position as they plan for life beyond Robert Lewandowski.Those links have existed since Haaland established himself as one of Europe's premier strikers and could become increasingly prominent if City's competitive level drops.A move to Madrid was even part of the platform of former Real Madrid presidential candidate Enrique Riquelme, who promised to sign Haaland had he won the club's election.He did not, leaving the situation unchanged for now.There is no indication that Haaland is currently pushing to leave City, and his enormous contract gives the club significant security. But Barry's argument is that circumstances, rather than the contract itself, could ultimately determine the striker's next move.If City continue challenging for major honours, there may be little reason for Haaland to look elsewhere. If that dominance begins to disappear, however, the equation changes.For a striker who has already achieved extraordinary numbers at the Etihad and who is entering what should be the prime years of his career, the next two seasons could tell City, and Haaland, whether the future is still in Manchester.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
