articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: Man Utd captain wins 2025/26 PFA Players' Player of the Year as Bunny Shaw wins women's award
articles.summary: Man Utd's Bruno Fernandes crowned PFA Player of the Year as Man City’s Bunny Shaw wins women’s award for second time; men's Young Player of the Year handed to Man City's Nico O'Reilly as Arsenal's Olivia Smith picks up women's prize; Sir Kenny Dalglish receives merit award
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned the men's PFA Players' Player of the Year for the 2025/26 season, as Manchester City's Bunny Shaw won the women's award for a second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcame a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earn a Champions League return.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE!
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals.

He said: "It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment."

The Portugal international is the Red Devils' first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009/10 and adds to his Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Manchester City sharpshooter Shaw, who was also recognised by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women's Player of the Year award for the second time.

The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again, having scored 21 goals on the way to a third straight Golden Boot and her maiden Women's Super League title.

O'Reilly and Smith scoop young player awards

Arsenal's Olivia Smith picked up the women's PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool and continued her form in the capital.

Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly was named men's PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze.

The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City team-mates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

O'Reilly said: "I had a great season. I'm very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I'm over the moon how it turned out."

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice, with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford striker Igor Thiago completing the team.

Mariona Caldentey, last year's PFA Women's Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo.

Dom Ballard, who joined Bristol City from Leyton Orient earlier this summer, claimed the award in League One, while Swindon striker Aaron Drinan picked up the League Two prize.

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football.

Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as a player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland's most capped player, having represented his country on 102 occasions.

The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June that he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn's Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup.

Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

articles.title: Ipswich Town 3-1 Leicester City: Marcelino Nunez's stunning strike from centre-circle send Tractor Boys through in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second round tie between Ipswich Town and Leicester City at Portman Road; Marcelino Nunez scored a contender for goal of the season as Gary O'Neil's side run out 3-1 winners
articles.body:
Marcelino Nunez scored a sensational goal from the halfway line to help Ipswich claim a hard-fought 3-1 win over Leicester in the Carabao Cup.

This had been a Premier League fixture only 15 months ago, but Leicester arrived at Portman Road fresh from a painful home loss to Burton in League One and yet under-fire Russell Martin watched the Foxes edge a goalless first half.

Sindre Walle Egeli showed Premier League quality for Gary O'Neil's team with a smart left-footed finish to break the deadlock after 62 minutes before 19-year-old Olabade Aluko earned Leicester a deserved leveller five minutes later.

  • How the teams lined up | Match stats
  • Latest news and rumours: Ipswich | Watch FREE PL highlights
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺

However, ex-Norwich midfielder Nunez fittingly had the final say in the meeting between two former Canaries team-mates.

Nunez rifled home off a post after 71 minutes to score for the first time at Portman Road since his move last summer and added a wonderful 50-yard lob in stoppage time to help Ipswich reach the Carabao Cup third round for only the second time in 11 seasons.

Martin was booed after Leicester lost to Burton and watched his team almost gift an opener inside 33 seconds, but Chuba Akpom could not profit.

Leicester, to their credit, quickly settled and Brighton loanee Tom Watson sent one shot wide before he tested Christian Walton with a curled effort.

Ipswich back-up goalkeeper Walton thwarted Christian McFarlane's attempted chip in the 20th minute after a lovely Louis Page pass and at the other end Jakub Stolarczyk made a fine save from Dara O'Shea's header.

However, Leicester finished the half strongly when Conor Chaplin's curler was pushed wide by Walton.

Ipswich midfielder Kasey McAteer had a goal ruled out for offside two minutes after half-time before Chaplin was withdrawn to a standing ovation on the hour mark by Martin, who then watched the home side break the deadlock in the 62nd minute.

Akpom played through to Jack Clarke and he squared for Egeli to slot home.

Five minutes later, Leicester equalised when Page's corner was flicked on by Bobby De Cordova-Reid and 19-year-old Aluko got a faint touch to score his first professional goal.

Nunez ensured there would be no upset when he fired in via a post after Woyo Coulibaly had given the ball away and after Akpom squandered a one-on-one chance, the Chile international grabbed a second.

After the ball dropped inside the centre circle, Nunez spotted Stolarczyk off his line and lobbed over the Leicester goalkeeper in incredible fashion to make it back-to-back wins for O'Neil.

The managers...

Ipswich's Gary O'Neil:

"I didn't think it was the best decision to be honest!

"Neither did Chuba (Akpom) or Sindre who were clean through on goal, but as long as you can put it in the goal no one can argue, so good decision in the end!

"The last two performances Marcelino has been excellent. Two great goals, unbelievable energy that he has, never stops and unbelievably humble kid that works and works.

"You need them in your group and two big moments of quality to add to that which changed the game for us.

"He is in a good spot and need to keep him going. We need to keep him going for the weekend and it is now a big push to get everyone going on Sunday (at Manchester United)."

Leicester's Russell Martin:

"The players were amazing and I loved it. I loved the performance.

"We were unlucky to lose and definitely unlucky to lose 3-1, but after Saturday we spoke a lot about bravery, aggression and intensity. With and without the ball they showed so much.

"The only thing missing is we didn't win but if we play like that, it is really exciting for us. We'll have a lot of fun and win a lot of games.

"It is so early and that is why I feel really calm about it. The fans were amazing as well. Hopefully they felt a bit of energy after that performance."

articles.title: LASK 5-1 Celtic (agg 5-4): Hoops throw away four-goal aggregate lead as stunning collapse ends Champions League group stage hopes
articles.summary: Report as Celtic are dumped out of the Champions League after throwing away a four-goal aggregate lead to LASK; Celtic took the lead on the night through Callum McGregor but LASK scored five to deny them a spot in Thursday's draw; Celtic to play Europa League football again
articles.body:
Celtic suffered a stunning Champions League play-off collapse as LASK overturned a 3-0 first-leg deficit to win 5-4 after extra-time and sent the Scottish champions crashing into the Europa League.

In one of the worst nights in Celtic's European history, the Hoops were up 4-0 on aggregate after Callum McGregor extended their 3-0 first-leg advantage early on in Austria.

Despite wobbling after goals from Moses Usor, Robert Ljubicic and a Samuel Adeniran stunner, Celtic were minutes from booking a place in Thursday's League phase draw before second-half substitute Florian Flecker headed home a 90th-minute equaliser to force extra-time.

  • How it happened | Teams | Stats
  • Watch FREE Scottish Prem highlights | Latest Scottish Prem news | Latest scores
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream the Scottish Prem with no contract

Full of all the energy and desire that Celtic whimpered at the sight of, the momentum belonged to the Austrian champions. Adeniran struck from range again in the 109th minute to put LASK in front on aggregate for the first time.

He very nearly added salt to Celtic's wounds when he stepped up for a penalty moments later, after Reo Hatate fouled Krystof Danek deep, but Viljami Sinisalo kept the spot-kick out to give his side a lifeline.

It was a lifeline that went begging as the full-time whistle confirmed Celtic would miss out on the Champions League for the second consecutive season. Last season it was defeat on penalties at this stage to Kairat Almaty.

This year's failure, given the context of a four-goal aggregate lead, will take considerably longer to move on from.

Once again the Hoops will be involved in the Europa League league-phase draw on Friday.

The key moments from Raiffeisen Arena

  • 6: BIG CHANCE! Celtic move it quickly up the field. Yang plays a ball into the area that Baur latches onto, poking wide of the mark with Hogh running in.

  • 20: LASK CHANCES! The first falls to Mbuyamba in the area, who can't quite match the flight of the ball to send it goalwards. Any touch on that and Lask would have had a goal. The second has Sinisalo worried, as it strikes the post.

  • 21: GOAL! It's a smart, smart low strike from McGregor but it takes a nick off Andrade and flies past Jungwirth in the LASK goal.

  • 32: GOAL! IT'S A GIFT! Celtic punished for complacent play at the back. Nygren passes a ball back into no man's land, putting it on a plate for Usor to stroke past Sinisalo.

  • 48: GOAL! LASK LEAD! Lask are beginning to believe. Ljubicic beats Sinisalo from range with a superb low strike from the edge of the area.

  • 58: GOAL! WHAT A FINISH!!! That is simply superb technique. No chance Sinisalo was getting anywhere near that. The LASK striker is teed up outside the box and curls home.

  • 90: GOAL! LASK MAKE IT FOUR TO SEND IT TO EXTRA TIME! Sinisalo does brilliantly to deny Joao Victor Tornich initially, but he can do nothing about the rebound as Florian Flecker heads home to make it 4-4 on aggregate!

  • 108: GOAL! Nightmare stuff for Celtic as Adeniran strikes from range again. LASK now lead on aggregate.

  • 114: FROM BAD TO WORSE! Hatate brings down Danek in the box gives away a penalty!

O'Neill: We should've been out of sight

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill speaking with Amazon Prime:

"We should've been out of sight by half-time. We missed two great opportunities and then we gave them a lifeline right before half-time and then another one just after it. They came roaring back. That's my team, that's my responsibility.

"At half-time I thought we were still well in command of the game. Just after they score and then momentum goes in their direction. It's hard to stem it when they're chasing the game and we can't get out for 10 minutes.

"These are tough games. This might have been a qualification game but it felt like a Champions League game. That doesn't matter. Talking about the squad is for another day.

"It's a massive disappointment. We're playing in the Europa League but that's no consolation this evening. There was a feel good factor and that's a massive disappointment tonight."

McGregor issues apology to Celtic fans

Celtic's Callum McGregor speaking with Amazon Prime:

"We got what we deserved. I thought we were passive all night. We actually looked scared to go and win the game.

"To be honest, I don't think we were that good in the first leg either and we kind of got away with it. But then you're up 3-0 and think you have a chance. When you play like that, you can't have any excuse whatsoever.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to the supporters and to the club because there's no way we should lose that game. Now we have to see what character we have.

"You can't lose the game by such a big margin and look for excuses elsewhere. This is where we see what people are made of in terms of what we achieve this season."

Your views: 'Celtic were hapless, hopeless and humiliated'

LJJ: "Absolutely embarrassing for Celtic, maybe Europa League is the level for them since they get into the CL with ease every year but don't make an impact when actually in it. Maybe that's their level, but I don't think they deserve Europe at all after what I've just witnessed!"

Jonny: "Celtic got what they deserved. They didn't exactly play well last week and were lucky to come away with three goals and decided to park the bus, just not good enough."

Reinaldo7: "Don't know whether to laugh or cry. Worse than last year against Kairat. Strange choices for subs tonight. Hang your heads in shame boys, they weren't that special but made us look ordinary. More work needed if we are to succeed in Europe."

Stevo: "I think this was worse than Kairat. Yes, it's not ideal losing on penalties to them, but to be 4-0 up and throw that all away, that's impressively shocking!"

jcluk: "No more LASK chances for Celtic. They were hapless, hopeless and humiliated. Can see them struggling domestically too this season."

What next for Celtic...

Celtic will play in the Europa League this season. The Europa League league phase draw - involving Bournemouth, Sunderland and Crystal Palace - takes place at 12pm UK time on Friday

articles.title: Jonas Urbig still has fondness for FC Köln, but Bayern Munich was perfect next step
articles.summary: Jonas Urbig cannot say enough about FC Bayern’s club environment.
articles.body:
After spending more than a decade at FC Köln, Jonas Urbig knew that moving to Bayern Munich would be a major change. But according to the young goalkeeper, settling in at his new club happened much faster than he expected.

Speaking to Bayern Munich's club magazine Säbener51, Urbig opened up about leaving Köln and discovering what life is really like inside Bayern Munich:

"I will always have an emotional connection with Köln. I wish the club nothing but the best – unless they are playing against us. At first, I only knew Bayern Munich from the outside. But once I got to know the club from within, I quickly realized how human and open everyone at the club is. From the outside, 'Mia San Mia' can often sound like just a slogan, but today I know that it is genuinely lived here. And that feels really good. That was certainly one of the reasons why I felt very quickly that I was in the right place here," Urbig said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

Urbig's comments offer an interesting perspective on the culture at Bayern Munich. From the outside, "Mia San Mia" can easily be viewed as nothing more than a famous club motto. For Urbig, however, experiencing the environment firsthand has given the phrase an entirely different meaning.

After more than ten years in Köln, leaving a club that played such an important role in his development could never be easy. But Urbig appears to have found a new home in Munich, surrounded by a group that has made him feel welcome from the beginning.

Now, his goal is to continue developing and prove that he belongs at Bayern Munich.

articles.title: LASK v Celtic: Martin O'Neill takes responsibility
articles.summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill says his team have a "million miles to go" after defeat in Austria.
articles.body:
In the open air of the Raiffeisen Arena, with bedlam all around, there was nowhere to hide for Celtic or Martin O'Neill.

The Scottish champions had endured one of the darkest nights in their European history.

After going out to Kairat Almaty on penalties last year at this stage of the Champions League play-offs, that is saying something.

Four goals up on aggregate against LASK, O'Neill's Celtic somehow conspired to implode in a second half with little sign of a response on the way to a 5-4 aggregate loss following extra time.

There was no hiding place, and the Celtic manager was frank when put in the spotlight at full-time.

"I'm responsible for this one," he said.

"Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the Uefa Cup final in 2003 but this was majorly disappointing.

"In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through.

"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."

Celtic blow four-goal lead to LASK in Champions League collapse

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded Published 4 hours ago

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded

O'Neill was not in charge for that defeat in Kazakhstan a year ago as it triggered the start of the end for Brendan Rodgers' second spell at Celtic Park.

The current Parkhead boss helped steady Celtic's ship last term following Rodgers' exit and again following the Wilfried Nancy saga to guide them to another league title and a Scottish Cup.

This season appeared to get off to a prosperous start until the roof began to cave in over in Austria.

Away from the raw pain of stumbling in such a stark way, the aftermath could be telling for Celtic who now have to not only pick themselves up, but finish off a transfer window without the hefty windfall which would have blown in with the Champions League.

"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," said O'Neill.

"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.

"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.

"That's not going to be the case but we'll see. Tonight we came up well and truly short, particularly in the second half."

Celtic captain Callum McGregor tells Amazon Prime: "We got what we deserved. We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.

"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game.

"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere.

"You'll now see what people are made of. When you play like that you can't have any excuses whatsoever.

"When you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, you can't have any excuse and that's on us.

"You fall at a big hurdle and these questions [on whether the squad are ready] are going to be asked. You can't lose by that margin then look for excuses elsewhere.

"This is what it's like to play at Celtic. You have to bounce back, you have to show a reaction and that's what Celtic are all about."

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown on BBC Radio Scotland: " It was a fantastic start, you go 1-0 up, but that seems like forever ago. Now they've crashed out the Champions League and conceded five goals.

"LASK outran Celtic in a couple of areas, the two up front were strong, solid and willing runners.

"LASK deserve to go through with that performance. I feel for the lads because I've been in that situation as well."

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Amazon Prime: "It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted. Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.

"They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."

Former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov: "Everyone [is to blame].

"They are all in it together. A big club like Celtic should be able to hold that out."

articles.title: Champions League 26/27 draw, dates, schedule, format and who has qualified from Premier League and around Europe
articles.summary: Arsenal, Man Utd , Liverpool, Man City and Aston Villa will all take part in the 2026/27 Champions League; draw for the league phase will take place in Monaco on Thursday
articles.body:
The league phase draw for the 2026/27 Champions League will take place on Thursday in Monaco and here is everything you need to know before it gets started.

How does the league phase draw work?

A total of 36 teams will enter the competition at this stage after 29 qualified at the end of last season. The remaining seven places are determined by the qualifiers.

In the new format, which is entering its third season since being implemented, teams now play fixtures against eight different teams - two teams from Pots 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Half of the eight league-phase matches are at home, with the other half away.

  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

The draw is done by a supercomputer, which automatically selects the eight opponents by one touch of a button.

Who is in each pot?

While four places via qualifiers are yet to be determined, 32 teams have been confirmed.

The pots are allocated based on UEFA's club coefficient rankings, which reflects results in European competitions across a five-year period ending in 2025/26.

Back-to-back champions Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Manchester City, Inter Milan, Arsenal, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid are in Pot 1.

Manchester United and Europa League winners Aston Villa, two clubs making their return to Europe's elite competition, have been placed in Pot 2.

Pot 1

  • PSG

  • Bayern Munich

  • Real Madrid

  • Liverpool

  • Inter Milan

  • Manchester City

  • Arsenal

  • Barcelona

  • Atletico Madrid

Pot 2

  • Aston Villa

  • Manchester United

  • Borussia Dortmund

  • Roma

  • Sporting

  • Porto

  • Club Brugge

  • PSV Eindhoven

  • Real Betis

Pot 3

  • Feyenoord

  • Lille

  • Napoli

  • RB Leipzig

  • Villarreal

  • Shakhtar Donetsk

  • Galatasaray

Pot 3 or 4 - to be decided

  • Bodo/Glimt

  • LASK Linz

  • Sabah

  • Slavia Prague

  • Stuttgart

  • Como

  • Lens

  • Winner of Fenerbahce vs Lyon

  • Winner of Dinamo Zagreb vs Viking

  • Winner of Slovan Bratislava vs Celje

  • Winner of Levski Sofia vs AEK Athens

Who qualifies for the knockout rounds?

The top eight sides in the league will qualify automatically for the round of 16, while teams finishing 25th or lower are eliminated and do not drop into the Europa League.

The teams finishing in ninth to 24th place compete in a two-legged knockout-phase play-off. Teams finishing between ninth and 16th are seeded, meaning they will face a team in 17th-24th with the return leg at home.

The eight clubs who win their knockout-phase play-off each meet one of the seeded top-eight finishers in the league-phase table for a place in the quarter-finals.

Champions League league-phase match dates and schedule

Matchday 1: September 8-10
Matchday 2: October 13/14
Matchday 3: October 20/21
Matchday 4: November 3/4
Matchday 5: November 24/25
Matchday 6: December 8/9
Matchday 7: January 19/20
Matchday 8: January 27

Champions League knockout-phase match dates and schedule

The draw for the two-legged knockout-phase play-offs is yet to be determined.

Knockout phase play-offs: February 16/17 and 23/24
Round of 16: March 9/10 and 16/17
Quarter-finals: April 6/7 and 13/14
Semi-finals: April 27/28 and May 4/5
Final: June 5

When are where is the final?

The final will take place at the Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, Spain, on June 5 2027.

articles.title: Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad: How to Watch Today as Madrid’s Injury Problems Grow
articles.summary: Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad takes place at the Santiago Bernabéu on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, in the rearranged La Liga Matchday 1 fixture. Kick-off is se...
articles.body:
Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad takes place at the Santiago Bernabéu on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, in the rearranged La Liga Matchday 1 fixture. Kick-off is set for 9:00 p.m. CEST, or 8:00 p.m. BST. Real Madrid will play their first home league game of the season after opening the campaign with a 2-1 win away to Espanyol.

Real Sociedad, meanwhile, arrive in Madrid after losing 1-0 to Real Betis . The fixture was moved from its original date because several Real Madrid players were still involved in the 2026 World Cup.

José Mourinho will lead Real Madrid into his first competitive home match since returning to the club. Pellegrino Matarazzo will take charge of Real Sociedad as both teams look to improve their early league position.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad will see Mourinho manage a squad affected by early injuries. Éder Militão and Rodrygo are unavailable, while Ferland Mendy , Raúl Asencio and Thiago Pitarch are also sidelined according to the match information supplied. Real Madrid started the season with a 2-1 win at Espanyol, with new signing Carlos Espí scoring the 90th-minute winner. Jude Bellingham had earlier put Madrid ahead before Espanyol equalized.

Real Sociedad began with a 1-0 defeat against Real Betis. Mikel Oyarzabal is among the key players available to Matarazzo, while Álvaro Odriozola remains out with a long-term knee injury. Gonçalo Guedes and Pablo Marín faced fitness checks before the match.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad Lineups and Key Numbers

The confirmed Real Madrid lineup includes Thibaut Courtois , Denzel Dumfries , Álvaro Carreras, Federico Valverde , Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen , Arda Güler, Bernardo Silva , Kylian Mbappé , Jude Bellingham and Vinícius Júnior . Mourinho has selected a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Real Sociedad's starting team includes Álex Remiro , Jon Aramburu , Sergio Gómez , Carlos Soler , Igor Zubeldia , Jon Martín, Takefusa Kubo , Yangel Herrera , Orri Steinn Óskarsson and Luka Sučić, with the final attacking position listed for Gonçalo Guedes in the confirmed lineup. Matarazzo also uses a 4-2-3-1 shape. Oyarzabal is among the substitutes.

Real Madrid have won four of their last five meetings with Real Sociedad. Their most recent meeting at the Bernabéu ended in a 4-1 Real Madrid victory in February 2026, with Vinícius Júnior scoring twice. The teams also played out a 4-4 Copa del Rey draw in April 2025.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad: How to Watch and Match Details

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad kicks off at 9:00 p.m. CEST at the Santiago Bernabéu. Real Madrid's official schedule confirms the match was postponed from Matchday 1 because of World Cup commitments.

In Spain , the match is listed on Orange TV and Movistar LaLiga. Viewers outside Spain can also follow the match through regional broadcasters. Fans in the UK can use Premier Sports or LaLigaTV, while DAZN has coverage in Italy and Germany .

In the US, ESPN+ and ESPN Deportes will carry La Liga, with TSN+ serving viewers in Canada . beIN Sports covers the Middle East and North Africa, while SuperSport provides La Liga coverage across Sub-Saharan Africa.
